item.title: @amitisinvesting: A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY. Here's a full recap: 1. Robinhood $HOOD reporte...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY.
Here's a full recap:
1. Robinhood $HOOD reported Q3 2026 revenue of $1.4B, up 12% YoY but slightly below the $1.42B estimate, while EPS of $0.51 missed expectations of $0.56, including a $0.07 per-share unrealized investment loss primarily tied to Robinhood Ventures Fund I. Net income declined 14% to $476M, while adjusted EBITDA increased 9% to $808M. Transaction-based revenue grew 19% to $867M, partially offset by a 9% decline in net interest revenue to $415M. Meanwhile, total platform assets climbed 19% to $396B, funded customers increased 7% to 28.7M, and Gold subscribers surged 34% to 5.2M, supported by $15.7B in net deposits. Robinhood now has 14 business lines generating over $100M in annualized revenue, with Rothera surpassing $100M in its first full quarter. CEO Vlad Tenev emphasized that customers are entrusting more assets to the platform as Robinhood expands its financial services ecosystem, although earnings growth continues to lag revenue growth.
2. SoFi $SOFI delivered a strong Q3 2026, with revenue surging 44% YoY to $1.4B, while adjusted EPS increased 64% to $0.18 and adjusted EBITDA jumped 70% to $469.8M, highlighting accelerating growth and improving profitability. Total members climbed 35% YoY to 17.1M, reflecting continued expansion across SoFi's financial services ecosystem. Looking ahead, the company issued bullish FY2027 guidance, projecting $6.4B in revenue versus $6B expected, EPS of $0.90 versus $0.82 expected, adjusted EBITDA of $2.24B, and net income of $1.28B. CEO Anthony Noto emphasized that SoFi is attracting more members, increasing the number of products used per customer, and generating more revenue per product, reinforcing management's confidence in the company's long-term growth and profitability trajectory.
3. Chinese technology giants Alibaba $BABA, Tencent, and ByteDance are reportedly seeking long-term memory supply agreements with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, according to Korean media, as demand for AI data center infrastructure continues to accelerate. While traditional memory supply contracts typically span 3–5 years, some Chinese cloud service providers are now requesting 10-year agreements extending through 2035 to secure access to critical DDR5 and LPDDR5 memory. The unusually long contract terms highlight growing concerns over future memory availability as hyperscalers expand AI computing capacity and compete for limited supply. The development could provide Samsung and SK Hynix with greater long-term revenue visibility and reinforces the structural demand outlook for the broader memory industry, including Micron $MU.
4. Meta $META has reportedly upsized its Class A common stock offering to $25B from $22.5B, pricing the shares at $625 each as the company raises additional capital to support its massive AI infrastructure expansion. Notably, NVIDIA $NVDA is investing $3B in the offering, while AMD $AMD is committing another $1B, giving two of Meta's major AI chip suppliers direct equity exposure to one of their largest customers. The expanded offering highlights Meta's increasingly aggressive capital-raising strategy as it prepares to spend $135B–$145B on capital expenditures in 2026. The participation of NVIDIA and AMD also underscores the growing financial interconnectedness of the AI ecosystem, with semiconductor suppliers investing directly in the hyperscalers purchasing their hardware.
5. Qualcomm $QCOM and Anduril are teaming up to launch BlueChip, a new venture focused on manufacturing rugged, waterproof, American-made laptops for the U.S. military, government agencies, law enforcement, and first responders, according to the Wall Street Journal. The devices will be assembled at Anduril's Arsenal-1 facility in Ohio and powered by Qualcomm Snapdragon X processors manufactured by TSMC in Arizona. Anduril founder Palmer Luckey said approximately 90% of the planned components already come from the U.S. and allied countries, with the long-term goal of producing the entire laptop domestically, including displays and other components currently sourced overseas. The initiative prioritizes secure computing, fully traceable supply chains, and reduced dependence on foreign manufacturing for national-security applications. The first laptops are expected in 2027, with pricing estimated at roughly 20% above conventional high-end PCs.
6. President Donald Trump made two major statements, reiterating his administration's decision to replace the terms “Artificial Intelligence” and “AI” with “Super Intelligence” and “SI” in official executive-branch communications, following a September executive order. Separately, Trump suggested that Venezuela could eventually become the 51st U.S. state, floating the possibility of replacing its presidency with a governorship during remarks in Corpus Christi, Texas. Trump also celebrated the U.S. military intervention in Venezuela and its subsequent oil agreement, describing the operation as a historic victory and highlighting expanded American access to Venezuelan oil reserves.
7. Tesla $TSLA rallied approximately 4% on Tuesday to $407.46, extending Monday's 5.2% gain as shares broke above key technical resistance levels. The rally was primarily fueled by Barclays upgrading Tesla to Overweight and raising its price target to $450 from $370, citing improving automotive demand, accelerating energy storage growth, and a potential merger with SpaceX $SPCX that could create a premium for Tesla shareholders. Meanwhile, Tesla's robotaxi expansion continues to gain momentum, with its Texas fleet reportedly exceeding 1,050 vehicles, Cybercabs outnumbering Model Ys, and additional service areas planned, including Dallas. Investors are also responding to improving FSD adoption, strong demand for energy storage from AI data centers, and signs of stabilization in Tesla's core automotive business.
8. Brazil's stock market experienced an extraordinary selloff on October 26, with the iShares MSCI Brazil ETF $EWZ plunging 19.8% in a single session, representing an estimated 8.4-standard-deviation move based on its historical daily volatility. Over the past 20 years, EWZ has averaged a daily return of approximately 0.04%, with a standard deviation of 2.36%, making Monday's decline an extreme statistical outlier. Under a theoretical normal distribution, a move of this magnitude would have an exceptionally small probability, illustrating just how unusual the selloff was relative to historical volatility. However, actual financial markets exhibit fat-tailed return distributions, meaning extreme declines occur more frequently than conventional statistical models predict. The plunge highlights the severity of the selling pressure in Brazilian equities and the risks associated with sudden market shocks.
9. Alphabet's $GOOGL Waymo is expanding its fully autonomous ride-hailing service by nearly 250 square miles across five existing U.S. markets over the next week, further accelerating its commercial robotaxi rollout. In Los Angeles, Waymo is extending service along the coast into the South Bay, including Torrance, while San Diego coverage will expand north to La Jolla, connecting riders to UC San Diego, the VA, and University Town Center. In Nashville, the company is expanding south to include Nashville Zoo, while Orlando will see its eastern service area nearly double alongside improved downtown coverage. The San Francisco Bay Area will also gain additional southern coverage, including a connection to Berryessa BART Station. The expansion increases Waymo's geographic reach and the number of destinations accessible to existing riders, rather than representing launches in five new cities, as Alphabet continues scaling its autonomous transportation network.
10. The top 10 most active options today by contracts traded were $NVDA with 2.4M contracts, $TSLA with 2.3M contracts, $AAPL with 1.2M contracts, $SOFI with 944K contracts, $SPCX with 852K contracts, $AMZN with 833K contracts, $MU with 716K contracts, $META with 709K contracts, $GOOGL with 529K contracts, and $AMD with 529K contracts.
11. Amazon $AMZN is reportedly working to reduce its reliance on Anthropic's AI models as the cost of operating Alexa+ continues to climb, according to Business Insider. Internal projections estimated that Alexa+ cloud computing expenses could reach approximately $1.7B in 2026, nearly triple the prior year's costs, prompting Amazon to explore routing more AI requests through its own lower-cost models and infrastructure. The company also considered delaying or scaling back Moonraker, its advanced AI agent initiative, which was projected to require more than $100M in GPU spending this year. The developments highlight the growing pressure on major technology companies to improve AI inference economics, reduce dependence on third-party model providers, and balance increasingly expensive AI capabilities with sustainable profitability.
12. U.S. stock market breadth is improving significantly, with the S&P 500 Equal-Weight Index outperforming the traditional market-cap-weighted S&P 500 by 4.0 percentage points in October, putting it on track for its second-strongest monthly relative performance since April 2009. The equal-weight index has gained 4.3% this month, compared with just 0.3% for the S&P 500, marking a sharp reversal from September, when equal-weight stocks underperformed by 4.7 percentage points, their worst relative month since March 2020. For comparison, the equal-weight index outperformed by 4.2 percentage points in April. Year-to-date, the Equal-Weight Index is up 13.4% versus 12.1% for the S&P 500, suggesting market leadership is broadening beyond the largest technology and AI companies as more sectors and individual stocks participate in the rally.
WALL STREET IS THE GREATEST SHOW ON EARTH.

item.title: @amitisinvesting: the $meta selloff due to equity dilution is really annoying but at the same time...can we really bl...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
the $meta selloff due to equity dilution is really annoying
but at the same time...can we really blame them?
meta and google both did equity raises this year for about $100B each. they are the greatest businesses in the world.
google is flat ytd and meta is now red after peaking at $780.
they have both been opportunity costs, but not because they are small spec plays that you took a chance on...these are some of the greatest businesses in the world.
the problem is, they need capital. they dont have fcf anymore. they levered up their balance sheets. the only thing left is equity to offer. if we want them to be the giant compounders that the global economy depends on, they need capital for their AI buildout and that capital will come from dilution which unfortunately keeps their stocks stuck.
ever since google did their raise, they have gone nowhere but flat to down, even berkshire is bagholding 10b of $googl they bought at 350.
the $meta $25b offering today at $625 was 5x oversubscribed, just like google's was, which means smart money obviously knows these are amazing discounts/valuations to pay...but the street isnt going to easily let these names run with the threat of more shares entering into the market.
the fact that $nvda and $amd had to invest in $meta today also shows how much the chipmakers realize that these companies need cash and they will have to participate in financing these companies to make sure their chip sales are disrupted.
this all doesn't work if the capex isn't going to lead to an roi. if it will, then i expect them to continue diluting and that means we might have to deal with the hyperscalers potentially being stuck if the street can't get over their constant dillution.
now, $amzn and $msft haven't tapped equity markets yet...which means if they do, we know the playbook for how the street may react. if they don't, then they might have a better chance of avoiding that stagnation, but ultimately if you believe in the AI buildout, these companies need money and that money will have to come from shareholders.
we just get the opportunity, even if prolonged, to buy them at what are historically the lowest multiples they've ever had relative to their growth with the eventual ROI from all this capex coming over the next few years.

the $meta $25b offering today at $625 was 5x oversubscribed, just like google's was, which means smart money obviously knows these are amazing discounts/valuations to pay...but the street isnt going to easily let these names run with the threat of more shares entering into the market.

the fact that $nvda and $amd had to invest in $meta today also shows how much the chipmakers realize that these companies need cash and they will have to participate in financing these companies to make sure their chip sales are disrupted.

this all doesn't work if the capex isn't going to lead to an roi. if it will, then i expect them to continue diluting and that means we might have to deal with the hyperscalers potentially being stuck if the street can't get over their constant dillution.

now, $amzn and $msft haven't tapped equity markets yet...which means if they do, we know the playbook for how the street may react. if they don't, then they might have a better chance of avoiding that stagnation, but ultimately if you believe in the AI buildout, these companies need money and that money will have to come from shareholders.

we just get the opportunity, even if prolonged, to buy them at what are historically the lowest multiples they've ever had relative to their growth with the eventual ROI from all this capex coming over the next few years.

LLMs are just commodity with no moat.

item.title: @amitisinvesting: A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY. Here's a full recap: 1. SpaceX $SPCX has signed...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY.
Here's a full recap:
1. SpaceX $SPCX has signed a binding commitment letter with an Apollo Global Management-managed entity for a massive $40B GPU financing arrangement to support its expanding AI data center infrastructure. Under the proposed agreement, Apollo's entity would purchase GPU pods and related data center equipment and lease them to SpaceX, with approximately $40B in aggregate principal payments spread across lease terms of 5 to 5.25 years. The transaction is expected to close before year-end, with GPU deliveries and lease payments beginning in the first half of 2027. Importantly, the $40B figure excludes interest and additional financing costs, with the final borrowing rate still to be determined, highlighting the enormous capital requirements behind SpaceX's AI infrastructure expansion.
2. Anthropic has reportedly filed its S-1 for a U.S. IPO, seeking to list on the Nasdaq under ticker $ANT, with Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and JPMorgan leading the offering. The filing shows explosive growth, with H1 2026 revenue surging to $16.3B from $1.16B a year earlier, including $13.1B in consumption-based revenue and $3.2B from subscriptions. Anthropic now has more than 11,900 customers spending $100K+ annually, including 1,900 spending over $1M and approximately 250 spending over $10M, while net revenue retention reached roughly 900% as of September 30. Despite the growth, Anthropic reported an $80.7B net loss, largely driven by a $72.4B noncash fair-value charge tied to convertible notes, while its operating loss narrowed to $693M. The biggest revelation is the company's enormous AI infrastructure commitments extending as far as 2045, including approximately $161B in Broadcom TPU leases, $120.5B with SpaceXAI, $114.5B with Google, $110B with Amazon, $44.9B with Microsoft, and tens of billions more with Nscale, Lambda, and AMD, alongside roughly $245B in additional agreements signed after June 30. Anthropic also disclosed $131.7B in cash and short-term investments, plans to allocate 5% of its shares to a public benefit fund, and a governance structure preserving 50.1% voting control for its founders, highlighting both the extraordinary scale of its growth and the capital intensity of the frontier AI industry.
3. Barclays upgraded Tesla $TSLA to Overweight from Equal Weight, raising its price target to $450 from $370, as analyst Dan Levy sees an increasingly attractive risk/reward profile. Levy noted that much of the recent discussion surrounding Tesla has focused on a potential merger with SpaceX $SPCX, which he believes could result in a premium for Tesla shareholders. However, his bullish thesis extends beyond a possible combination, citing improving automotive demand, strong growth in Tesla's energy business, and a sharp acceleration in Robotaxi miles driven. Barclays also highlighted FSD adoption exceeding 75% of new North American vehicle deliveries, suggesting growing monetization opportunities for Tesla's autonomous driving technology. Together, these factors underpin the firm's more constructive outlook on Tesla's long-term growth potential.
4. Microsoft $MSFT is offering voluntary buyouts to approximately 60,000 employees, representing more than 25% of its global workforce, as the company moves to restructure parts of its operations. The program reportedly covers select teams across the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, and India, with eligible employees receiving severance packages in exchange for voluntarily leaving the company. Employees have until early December to decide whether to participate, with departures expected to take place by year-end. The move could represent one of Microsoft's largest workforce restructuring initiatives, although the final number of departures will depend on employee participation.
5. Samsung and SK Hynix are reportedly targeting Q2 2027 to begin mass production and shipments of 8-layer HBM4 memory for NVIDIA $NVDA, according to ZDNet Korea. The advanced memory is expected to be used in NVIDIA's next-generation Rubin Ultra rack-scale AI systems, supporting the growing memory requirements of increasingly powerful AI accelerators. While 12-layer HBM4 remains the primary focus throughout 2026, the share of 8-layer HBM4 shipments is expected to increase significantly beginning in mid-2027. The development highlights the continued expansion of the high-bandwidth memory market as Samsung and SK Hynix prepare additional capacity for NVIDIA's next generation of AI infrastructure.
6. The top 10 most active options today by contracts traded were $TSLA with 3.4M contracts, $NVDA with 3.1M contracts, $AAPL with 1.6M contracts, $MU with 1.3M contracts, $SPCX with 1.3M contracts, $META with 979K contracts, $AMZN with 884K contracts, $NFLX with 624K contracts, $INTC with 598K contracts, and $AMD with 550K contracts.
7. Meta $META announced plans to raise approximately $35B through new equity offerings, including $22.5B in Class A common stock through forward sale agreements and $12.5B in depositary shares tied to mandatory convertible preferred stock. The company is also considering a separate $60B offering program for its new nonvoting Class C shares beginning in Q1 2027, potentially bringing its total equity financing capacity to $95B, approximately $10B more than Google's $85B equity offering earlier this year. Interestingly, NVIDIA $NVDA, AMD $AMD, and Broadcom $AVGO have expressed nonbinding interest in purchasing up to $5B of Meta shares combined, potentially giving major AI chip suppliers direct equity exposure to one of their largest customers. The proposed financing comes as Meta prepares for unprecedented AI infrastructure spending, while its new Class C share structure, introduced alongside an effective 2-for-1 stock split, would allow the company to raise additional capital without issuing new voting rights. The full $95B remains potential financing capacity rather than a completed capital raise.
8. DoorDash $DASH is reportedly in advanced negotiations to acquire Instacart $CART, with a potential agreement expected as early as this week, according to the Wall Street Journal. The discussions follow earlier reports that Instacart had attracted takeover interest from both DoorDash and Uber $UBER, although talks with Uber are reportedly no longer active. A combination would significantly expand DoorDash's presence in online grocery delivery, combining Instacart's grocery partnerships and fulfillment technology with DoorDash's restaurant delivery network and logistics infrastructure. The potential acquisition could strengthen DoorDash's competitive position across local commerce, although no final agreement has been announced and negotiations could still fall apart.
9. The 10 largest U.S. leveraged equity ETFs attracted approximately $12B in net inflows over the past month, even as their combined market capitalization declined by $20B, highlighting aggressive dip-buying despite the broader market selloff. The surge was led by the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF $SOXL, which attracted a record $9B in inflows over just two weeks, while the ProShares UltraPro QQQ $TQQQ, which provides 3x leveraged exposure to the Nasdaq 100, recorded $1.3B in inflows, its second-largest two-week intake of 2026. Over the past five months, the 10 largest leveraged equity ETFs have collectively attracted $19B, suggesting that speculative investors are continuing to increase leveraged exposure to semiconductors and technology stocks even as market volatility and downside risks remain elevated.
10. Morgan Stanley strategist Michael Wilson expects the current U.S. equity market correction to eventually give way to a rebound as several major uncertainties begin to clear, including the midterm elections, AI infrastructure financing concerns, and tightening financial conditions. Wilson sees potential near-term downside for the S&P 500 $SPX to 7,100–7,200, but maintains a year-end base-case target of 8,000, suggesting meaningful recovery potential if market conditions improve. He identified liquidity constraints as the biggest immediate risk, while arguing that a potential Federal Reserve policy pivot could provide an important catalyst for equities. Morgan Stanley also pointed to historically strong 6–12-month stock market returns following midterm elections, supporting its view that the current correction could ultimately create buying opportunities rather than mark the end of the broader market cycle.
11. UBS pushed back against concerns that CoreWeave $CRWV could face a debt spiral as credit markets tighten, arguing that the company has multiple financing alternatives to support its AI infrastructure expansion. UBS highlighted opportunities to reduce reliance on traditional debt through private credit, vendor financing, and additional equity investments, similar to CoreWeave's recent transaction with Jane Street. Following meetings with private credit executives and data center developers, UBS said it “did NOT come away with a view that capital will be scarce in 2027,” suggesting financing conditions may remain more supportive than investors fear. Separately, Cantor Fitzgerald reiterated its Overweight rating and $176 price target on CoreWeave, citing the potential for delayed-draw term loan (DDTL) credit enhancements to attract additional lenders and new financing facilities to ease concerns over the company's access to capital.
12. The United States and Canada are reportedly negotiating a potential agreement to ease tariffs on Canadian steel and automobiles, according to Reuters, citing six sources familiar with the discussions. Negotiations are focused on Section 232 tariffs, including duties of up to 50% on Canadian steel and 25% on automobiles, with one Canadian source suggesting a deal could be reached before the November 3 midterm elections. U.S. officials are reportedly seeking additional concessions from Canada. The discussions come as President Trump has threatened to raise steel and auto tariffs to 50% beginning January 1, 2027, although he recently suggested the trade dispute could be resolved “soon.” Canadian officials described the negotiations as constructive, but no agreement has been finalized.
WALL STREET IS THE GREATEST SHOW ON EARTH.

Under the proposed agreement, Apollo's entity would purchase GPU pods and related data center equipment and lease them to SpaceX, with approximately $40B in aggregate principal payments spread across lease terms of 5 to 5.25 years. The transaction is expected to close before year-end, with GPU deliveries and lease payments beginning in the first half of 2027. Importantly, the $40B figure excludes interest and additional financing costs, with the final borrowing rate still to be determined, highlighting the enormous capital requirements behind SpaceX's AI infrastructure expansion.

2. Anthropic has reportedly filed its S-1 for a U.S. IPO, seeking to list on the Nasdaq under ticker $ANT, with Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and JPMorgan leading the offering. The filing shows explosive growth, with H1 2026 revenue surging to $16.3B from $1.16B a year earlier, including $13.1B in consumption-based revenue and $3.2B from subscriptions. Anthropic now has more than 11,900 customers spending $100K+ annually, including 1,900 spending over $1M and approximately 250 spending over $10M, while net revenue retention reached roughly 900% as of September 30. Despite the growth, Anthropic reported an $80.7B net loss, largely driven by a $72.4B noncash fair-value charge tied to convertible notes, while its operating loss narrowed to $693M. The biggest revelation is the company's enormous AI infrastructure commitments extending as far as 2045, including approximately $161B in Broadcom TPU leases, $120.5B with SpaceXAI, $114.5B with Google, $110B with Amazon, $44.9B with Microsoft, and tens of billions more with Nscale, Lambda, and AMD, alongside roughly $245B in additional agreements signed after June 30. Anthropic also disclosed $131.7B in cash and short-term investments, plans to allocate 5% of its shares to a public benefit fund, and a governance structure preserving 50.1% voting control for its founders, highlighting both the extraordinary scale of its growth and the capital intensity of the frontier AI industry.

3. Barclays upgraded Tesla $TSLA to Overweight from Equal Weight, raising its price target to $450 from $370, as analyst Dan Levy sees an increasingly attractive risk/reward profile. Levy noted that much of the recent discussion surrounding Tesla has focused on a potential merger with SpaceX $SPCX, which he believes could result in a premium for Tesla shareholders. However, his bullish thesis extends beyond a possible combination, citing improving automotive demand, strong growth in Tesla's energy business, and a sharp acceleration in Robotaxi miles driven. Barclays also highlighted FSD adoption exceeding 75% of new North American vehicle deliveries, suggesting growing monetization opportunities for Tesla's autonomous driving technology. Together, these factors underpin the firm's more constructive outlook on Tesla's long-term growth potential.

4. Microsoft $MSFT is offering voluntary buyouts to approximately 60,000 employees, representing more than 25% of its global workforce, as the company moves to restructure parts of its operations. The program reportedly covers select teams across the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, and India, with eligible employees receiving severance packages in exchange for voluntarily leaving the company. Employees have until early December to decide whether to participate, with departures expected to take place by year-end. The move could represent one of Microsoft's largest workforce restructuring initiatives, although the final number of departures will depend on employee participation.

5. Samsung and SK Hynix are reportedly targeting Q2 2027 to begin mass production and shipments of 8-layer HBM4 memory for NVIDIA $NVDA, according to ZDNet Korea. The advanced memory is expected to be used in NVIDIA's next-generation Rubin Ultra rack-scale AI systems, supporting the growing memory requirements of increasingly powerful AI accelerators. While 12-layer HBM4 remains the primary focus throughout 2026, the share of 8-layer HBM4 shipments is expected to increase significantly beginning in mid-2027. The development highlights the continued expansion of the high-bandwidth memory market as Samsung and SK Hynix prepare additional capacity for NVIDIA's next generation of AI infrastructure.

6. The top 10 most active options today by contracts traded were $TSLA with 3.4M contracts, $NVDA with 3.1M contracts, $AAPL with 1.6M contracts, $MU with 1.3M contracts, $SPCX with 1.3M contracts, $META with 979K contracts, $AMZN with 884K contracts, $NFLX with 624K contracts, $INTC with 598K contracts, and $AMD with 550K contracts.

7. Meta $META announced plans to raise approximately $35B through new equity offerings, including $22.5B in Class A common stock through forward sale agreements and $12.5B in depositary shares tied to mandatory convertible preferred stock. The company is also considering a separate $60B offering program for its new nonvoting Class C shares beginning in Q1 2027, potentially bringing its total equity financing capacity to $95B, approximately $10B more than Google's $85B equity offering earlier this year. Interestingly, NVIDIA $NVDA, AMD $AMD, and Broadcom $AVGO have expressed nonbinding interest in purchasing up to $5B of Meta shares combined, potentially giving major AI chip suppliers direct equity exposure to one of their largest customers. The proposed financing comes as Meta prepares for unprecedented AI infrastructure spending, while its new Class C share structure, introduced alongside an effective 2-for-1 stock split, would allow the company to raise additional capital without issuing new voting rights. The full $95B remains potential financing capacity rather than a completed capital raise.

8. DoorDash $DASH is reportedly in advanced negotiations to acquire Instacart $CART, with a potential agreement expected as early as this week, according to the Wall Street Journal. The discussions follow earlier reports that Instacart had attracted takeover interest from both DoorDash and Uber $UBER, although talks with Uber are reportedly no longer active. A combination would significantly expand DoorDash's presence in online grocery delivery, combining Instacart's grocery partnerships and fulfillment technology with DoorDash's restaurant delivery network and logistics infrastructure. The potential acquisition could strengthen DoorDash's competitive position across local commerce, although no final agreement has been announced and negotiations could still fall apart.

9. The 10 largest U.S. leveraged equity ETFs attracted approximately $12B in net inflows over the past month, even as their combined market capitalization declined by $20B, highlighting aggressive dip-buying despite the broader market selloff. The surge was led by the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF $SOXL, which attracted a record $9B in inflows over just two weeks, while the ProShares UltraPro QQQ $TQQQ, which provides 3x leveraged exposure to the Nasdaq 100, recorded $1.3B in inflows, its second-largest two-week intake of 2026. Over the past five months, the 10 largest leveraged equity ETFs have collectively attracted $19B, suggesting that speculative investors are continuing to increase leveraged exposure to semiconductors and technology stocks even as market volatility and downside risks remain elevated.

10. Morgan Stanley strategist Michael Wilson expects the current U.S. equity market correction to eventually give way to a rebound as several major uncertainties begin to clear, including the midterm elections, AI infrastructure financing concerns, and tightening financial conditions. Wilson sees potential near-term downside for the S&P 500 $SPX to 7,100–7,200, but maintains a year-end base-case target of 8,000, suggesting meaningful recovery potential if market conditions improve. He identified liquidity constraints as the biggest immediate risk, while arguing that a potential Federal Reserve policy pivot could provide an important catalyst for equities. Morgan Stanley also pointed to historically strong 6–12-month stock market returns following midterm elections, supporting its view that the current correction could ultimately create buying opportunities rather than mark the end of the broader market cycle.

11. UBS pushed back against concerns that CoreWeave $CRWV could face a debt spiral as credit markets tighten, arguing that the company has multiple financing alternatives to support its AI infrastructure expansion. UBS highlighted opportunities to reduce reliance on traditional debt through private credit, vendor financing, and additional equity investments, similar to CoreWeave's recent transaction with Jane Street. Following meetings with private credit executives and data center developers, UBS said it “did NOT come away with a view that capital will be scarce in 2027,” suggesting financing conditions may remain more supportive than investors fear. Separately, Cantor Fitzgerald reiterated its Overweight rating and $176 price target on CoreWeave, citing the potential for delayed-draw term loan (DDTL) credit enhancements to attract additional lenders and new financing facilities to ease concerns over the company's access to capital.

12. The United States and Canada are reportedly negotiating a potential agreement to ease tariffs on Canadian steel and automobiles, according to Reuters, citing six sources familiar with the discussions. Negotiations are focused on Section 232 tariffs, including duties of up to 50% on Canadian steel and 25% on automobiles, with one Canadian source suggesting a deal could be reached before the November 3 midterm elections. U.S. officials are reportedly seeking additional concessions from Canada. The discussions come as President Trump has threatened to raise steel and auto tariffs to 50% beginning January 1, 2027, although he recently suggested the trade dispute could be resolved “soon.” Canadian officials described the negotiations as constructive, but no agreement has been finalized.

WALL STREET IS THE GREATEST SHOW ON EARTH.

item.title: @amitisinvesting: ANTHROPIC'S IPO DOCUMENTS ARE CALMING DOWN THE MARKETS. None of the numbers released today are that...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
ANTHROPIC'S IPO DOCUMENTS ARE CALMING DOWN THE MARKETS.
None of the numbers released today are that different from what we heard last week, but now we know how much cash they have.
Anthropic has $120B in cash and is likely raising $100B on the IPO. They are then likely going to be raising another $100B in debt, $60B of it already financed by BlackStone. If you assume a 3x in ARR, which probably is low considering how much the street wants them to grow, this company should have around $300-$400B in cash. This also doesn't take into account the future ATMs they might engage in.
So, the reason AI stocks are getting some relief right now is because it seems like Anthropic will have enough cash to pay their bills, which obviously is good for $NVDA, $SPCX, $AMD, $AVGO, $MU, and many other players.
However, there are going to be 24 separate unlocks in 2027. Those are going to be days where the market has to deal with a massive amount of supply coming onto the market. The company effectively has unilateral control, not shareholders, on deciding to pause or slow down the release of models. The open-weight models continue to be a threat as more enterprises are seeing the value in owning their AI for a significantly cheaper cost. Anthropic has outlined all these risks in the S1.
Regardless on if you are buying the IPO, it seems like there is enough cash they can raise to continue paying their bills and making sure the downstream value flows into most of the semis...if the market changes their mind on that or Anthropic stalls in growth, those names get hit. But if the company keeps growing and raises cash, the money should be there to fund the semis...it's now a question on how much of a risk people want to take in actually owning the stock.

ANTHROPIC'S IPO DOCUMENTS ARE CALMING DOWN THE MARKETS.

None of the numbers released today are that different from what we heard last week, but now we know how much cash they have.

Anthropic has $120B in cash and is likely raising $100B on the IPO. They are then likely going to be raising another $100B in debt, $60B of it already financed by BlackStone. If you assume a 3x in ARR, which probably is low considering how much the street wants them to grow, this company should have around $300-$400B in cash. This also doesn't take into account the future ATMs they might engage in.

So, the reason AI stocks are getting some relief right now is because it seems like Anthropic will have enough cash to pay their bills, which obviously is good for $NVDA, $SPCX, $AMD, $AVGO, $MU, and many other players.

However, there are going to be 24 separate unlocks in 2027. Those are going to be days where the market has to deal with a massive amount of supply coming onto the market. The company effectively has unilateral control, not shareholders, on deciding to pause or slow down the release of models. The open-weight models continue to be a threat as more enterprises are seeing the value in owning their AI for a significantly cheaper cost. Anthropic has outlined all these risks in the S1.

Regardless on if you are buying the IPO, it seems like there is enough cash they can raise to continue paying their bills and making sure the downstream value flows into most of the semis...if the market changes their mind on that or Anthropic stalls in growth, those names get hit. But if the company keeps growing and raises cash, the money should be there to fund the semis...it's now a question on how much of a risk people want to take in actually owning the stock.

item.title: @I_Am_The_ICT: Ladies & Gentlemen... If you never read another post or lend your attention my way, take these word...
item.dc:creator: @I_Am_The_ICT
item.description:
Ladies & Gentlemen...
If you never read another post or lend your attention my way, take these words to heart.
The opinions, of others about you, should never shape who you are. If you live your life like that, you will be led by emotions.
Greed and the pursuit to always please, impress, perform, or outclass someone else or something is a fools errand.
You won't convince everyone and no matter how many people claim to love you, believe in you, support you, promote you or what you stand for... the one person who doesn't and their weak words will disrupt your life.
None of you hold that measure of influence over me. Yet, I see so many falling into traps via greed and image building .
I hold a seat of influence most would abuse. A younger me might have abused it, I readily admit that. You might read the trolls say I only trade paper accounts, I never trade live for others to copy me.
I can stand here among others who open themselves up to legal troubles by doing otherwise... and I say, I warned you.
I want each of you to find a model that works for you. I would be thrilled to see all of you make millions. However, the truth is, most of you are ill equipped to do it consistently.
Anyone who sits in front of others and leads them in live executions, opens themselves a direct pathway, in legal terms, for those who pay you.
Some of you laugh at my teaching style in paper trading, but you don't assume liability in demo accounts. You never assume liability when you never provide "copy me" conditions for people who lack self-control or who are unable to manage impulsive behaviors.
You never assume liability if you don't sell affilate income with questionable practices.
I could have made more than all of the well known affiliate influencers combined, but I know the risks. I never held or accepted an affiliate partnership that benefited me money wise.
Unfortunately, some of you who laughed under your breath, in my direction, will learn why I operate the way I do.
Don't allow money to influence commonsense and good judgement.
A life with stress with lots of money in the bank is a broke life, so listen to good medicine.
Hope this helps someone...
item.content:encoded:
Ladies & Gentlemen...

If you never read another post or lend your attention my way, take these words to heart.

The opinions, of others about you, should never shape who you are. If you live your life like that, you will be led by emotions.

Greed and the pursuit to always please, impress, perform, or outclass someone else or something is a fools errand.

You won't convince everyone and no matter how many people claim to love you, believe in you, support you, promote you or what you stand for... the one person who doesn't and their weak words will disrupt your life.

None of you hold that measure of influence over me. Yet, I see so many falling into traps via greed and image building .

I hold a seat of influence most would abuse. A younger me might have abused it, I readily admit that. You might read the trolls say I only trade paper accounts, I never trade live for others to copy me.

I can stand here among others who open themselves up to legal troubles by doing otherwise... and I say, I warned you.

I want each of you to find a model that works for you. I would be thrilled to see all of you make millions. However, the truth is, most of you are ill equipped to do it consistently.

Anyone who sits in front of others and leads them in live executions, opens themselves a direct pathway, in legal terms, for those who pay you.

Some of you laugh at my teaching style in paper trading, but you don't assume liability in demo accounts. You never assume liability when you never provide "copy me" conditions for people who lack self-control or who are unable to manage impulsive behaviors.

You never assume liability if you don't sell affilate income with questionable practices.

I could have made more than all of the well known affiliate influencers combined, but I know the risks. I never held or accepted an affiliate partnership that benefited me money wise.

Unfortunately, some of you who laughed under your breath, in my direction, will learn why I operate the way I do.

Don't allow money to influence commonsense and good judgement.

A life with stress with lots of money in the bank is a broke life, so listen to good medicine.

Hope this helps someone...

S&P 500 book depth is looking pretty healthy here with lots of open orders.
For those who don't know, book depth tends to stabilize markets because a larger amount of open orders absorbs selling pressure.
Thin book depth is when you tend to see liquidity issues and flushes in the market.

the question is if those catalysts are enough to actually wreck the entire AI trade and if they arent...when do funds stop derisking and take advantage of discounts
to assume these aren't discounts and that this selloff will continue would be to assume that the buildout is entering peak earnings and now future cashflows should be further discounted
which is why inflows are just rotating to other elements of the S&P that aren't as affected by AI
if not, then there are many things on sale

item.title: @amitisinvesting: A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY. Here's a full recap: 1. The Nasdaq $QQQ was dow...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY.
Here's a full recap:
1. The Nasdaq $QQQ was down 2.60% on today, its worst session since June 5, while the Nasdaq 100 fell 2.90%, erasing nearly $1.2T in market value. The selloff was fueled by concerns over AI spending and profitability, with Meta $META dropping 7% despite beating revenue expectations, as investors questioned its massive AI investments and negative free cash flow. Semiconductors were hit hardest, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index falling 6.7%, led by AMD $AMD (-8%), Micron $MU (-6%), and NVIDIA $NVDA (-4%). AI and chip stocks accounted for roughly 90% of the Nasdaq 100's losses. However, broader market participation remained positive, with the Dow and Russell 2000 gaining. Meanwhile, Brent crude surged 4% toward $113 amid Middle East tensions. Despite the decline, the Nasdaq remains up 11.9% YTD, sitting 5.8% below its October 6 record high.
2. NVIDIA $NVDA CEO Jensen Huang pushed back against concerns surrounding neocloud financing, arguing that demand for AI computing infrastructure remains “off the charts” and that strong customer demand will ultimately help companies secure the capital needed to expand. Huang emphasized that “you can't solve the absence of demand,” but when demand is high, financing challenges can be addressed. He noted that neocloud providers already have excellent customers and significant demand, with their primary challenge being access to working capital to fund additional compute capacity. Huang expressed confidence that financing solutions will emerge, reinforcing his view that the industry's biggest challenge is not finding customers, but securing the capital and infrastructure needed to meet accelerating AI demand.
3. Bloom Energy $BE delivered a massive Q3 2026 earnings beat, with revenue surging 138% YoY to $1.24B, well above the $1.05B estimate, while adjusted EPS of $0.94 exceeded expectations of $0.68. Adjusted operating income reached $285.7M, beating the $214M estimate, while adjusted gross margins expanded 412 basis points to 34.5%, reflecting significant improvements in profitability. The company also raised its FY2026 revenue guidance to $4.4B–$4.6B, above the $4.1B consensus, and increased its adjusted EPS outlook to $3.10–$3.40, compared with $2.73 expected. Despite the strong results, operating cash flow was negative $27.1M during the quarter.
4. OpenAI is reportedly nearing a $30B funding round at a $1.25T valuation, with UAE investors and Coatue Management leading the financing, according to CNBC. The round is being positioned as a bridge ahead of a potential 2027 IPO, with OpenAI targeting investor signatures by the end of next week, although the final fundraising amount remains subject to change. Separately, OpenAI is negotiating an additional agreement to secure AI computing capacity from the UAE, highlighting the company's continued need for massive infrastructure investment as it scales its frontier AI models and expands its commercial operations. If completed at the proposed valuation, the financing would further cement OpenAI's position among the world's most valuable private technology companies.
5. SK Hynix has reportedly scrapped plans for a U.S. IPO of its Solidigm subsidiary and halted a related pre-IPO investment round following regulatory concerns and shareholder opposition, according to Bloomberg. South Korean regulators argued that separately listing the company's flash-memory business could constitute a “duplicate listing,” potentially diluting the economic interests of existing SK Hynix shareholders. The proposed IPO, which had Goldman Sachs $GS and Morgan Stanley $MS lined up as lead underwriters, was previously targeted for 2027. The decision represents a significant development in South Korea's efforts to strengthen minority shareholder protections and address the longstanding “Korea discount,” as regulators increasingly scrutinize corporate structures that could disadvantage existing public shareholders.
6. The top 10 most active options today by contracts traded were $NVDA with 3.5M contracts, $TSLA with 2.6M contracts, $SPCX with 1.7M contracts, $AAPL with 1.4M contracts, $MU with 1.2M contracts, $META with 1.2M contracts, $INTC with 1.2M contracts, $AMZN with 1.0M contracts, $NFLX with 967K contracts, and $CRWV with 941K contracts.
7. SpaceX $SPCX is reportedly seeking access to at least 80,000 cell tower sites across the United States as it accelerates plans to turn Starlink into a fourth nationwide wireless carrier, according to Bloomberg. The company is in discussions with major tower operators, including Crown Castle $CCI, over potential agreements that could be worth billions of dollars. The push follows SpaceX's recent acquisition agreement for nationwide low-band spectrum and FCC approval for a constellation of 15,000 direct-to-device satellites, giving Starlink the foundation to combine satellite connectivity with terrestrial cellular infrastructure. If successful, the expansion would position SpaceX to compete more directly with AT&T $T, Verizon $VZ, and T-Mobile $TMUS, potentially reshaping the U.S. wireless market.
8. China is continuing to accumulate significant amounts of gold, with Goldman Sachs estimating that Chinese purchases through the London OTC market reached 25 tonnes in August, approximately 25% above the 20 tonnes officially reported by China's central bank. The bank estimates China purchased 35 tonnes in July, 40 tonnes in June, and 48 tonnes in May, with estimated OTC purchases exceeding officially reported central bank purchases by 83 tonnes, or 128%, over the four-month period. Meanwhile, global central banks are estimated to have purchased 79 tonnes of gold in August, roughly 365% above the pre-2022 monthly average of 17 tonnes. The figures highlight exceptionally strong demand for gold amid ongoing geopolitical uncertainty, reserve diversification, and efforts by central banks to reduce reliance on traditional reserve assets, although estimated OTC purchases are not necessarily all central bank acquisitions.
9. NVIDIA $NVDA CEO Jensen Huang told CNBC that he believes a surplus of memory supply is unlikely by 2029, signaling continued confidence in long-term demand for DRAM, HBM, and other advanced memory technologies as AI infrastructure expands. Huang emphasized that “one of the things that’s really great about memory is that you can always use more of it,” highlighting how increasingly sophisticated AI models, larger context windows, and more demanding inference workloads continue to drive memory requirements higher.
10. SpaceX $SPCX is reportedly finalizing a $40B debt financing package at significantly higher borrowing costs than its previous financing, according to Semafor. The deal, led by Apollo and Goldman Sachs, is expected to include a lower-rated tranche carrying an interest rate of approximately 8.3%, while a more secure portion backed by AI chips could price around 7.75%. Even the chip-backed debt is expected to carry a yield more than 100 basis points above SpaceX's existing bonds, highlighting the rising cost of financing large-scale AI infrastructure. The transaction is expected to close next week and underscores the growing financial burden associated with SpaceX's aggressive expansion into AI computing and data centers.
11. Nebius $NBIS secured a $3.5B senior secured credit facility from Citi to finance its accelerating global AI data center expansion and GPU purchases. The facility carries a 364-day maturity, with borrowing costs starting at SOFR + 2.75% and potentially increasing to SOFR + 3.50%, giving Nebius additional access to capital as it scales its infrastructure. The company also highlighted more than $40B in long-term contracts with investment-grade customers, which could support further asset-backed financing as it expands AI computing capacity throughout 2027 and beyond. The agreement underscores how neocloud providers are increasingly leveraging contracted AI demand to secure billions in financing for next-generation data centers and GPU infrastructure.
12. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield fell below 5.00% for the first time since September 23, as the selloff in technology and AI-related stocks intensified. The decline in yields suggests investors are rotating capital toward the relative safety of U.S. government bonds, pushing Treasury prices higher as risk appetite weakens. The move highlights a growing divergence between the bond and equity markets, with falling yields reflecting demand for defensive assets even as concerns over AI valuations, capital spending, and broader market volatility continue to pressure technology stocks.
WALL STREET IS THE GREATEST SHOW ON EARTH.

The one thing I'm watching closely right now is what happened to the markets back in January 2025.
This scenario would make sense given the Nasdaq 100 Equal Weight Index is on support that ends around November 20th.
If the Dow repeated the January 2025 pattern that would mean markets would remain flat until OpEx on November 20th before selling off into January 2027.
The Dow's recent strength is suggesting this is possible.

In 2020 markets bounced for 3 weeks before rolling over again.
Either way, the 60 week moving average is clearly rolling over here, so the market top is in.

item.dc:creator: @charliebilello
item.description: Meta Q3 revenues increased 26% over the last year to a new record high of $64.6 billion. But costs/expenses rose 68% YoY to a record $51.6 billion ($9.9 billion of this was part of the $18.6 billion settlement related to teen mental health/social media). As a result, income from operations fell 37% YoY to $13 billion. And operating profit margins moved down to 20% from 40% a year ago. $META

item.title: @amitisinvesting: $META META Q3 2026 EARNINGS: - Revenue $64.6B +26% YoY - Advertising Revenue $63.1B +26% YoY - GAAP...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
$META
META Q3 2026 EARNINGS:
- Revenue $64.6B +26% YoY - Advertising Revenue $63.1B +26% YoY - GAAP Net Income $9.86B +264% YoY - Daily Active People 3.64B +3% YoY - Ad Impressions +10% YoY - Average Price Per Ad +14% YoY - Operating Cash Flow $32.8B - FY26 CapEx Guidance $135B-$145B
Meta announced plans for an effective 2-for-1 stock split in January 2027. Rather than simply doubling existing shares, Meta will issue one new publicly traded, non-voting Class C share for every existing Class A or Class B share. This means shareholders will receive an additional share without changing their voting power.
This also means Meta will likely do an equity raise, but if they can continue putting up numbers like this, the street will have to digest it.
Mark Zuckerberg:
"We hit major milestones this quarter toward delivering personal superintelligence for everyone - including launching Muse and Muse Wonder, our first frontier model. Our investments are paying off, the core business is strong, and we're seeing velocity across the board."
item.content:encoded:
$META

META Q3 2026 EARNINGS:

- Revenue $64.6B +26% YoY
- Advertising Revenue $63.1B +26% YoY
- GAAP Net Income $9.86B +264% YoY
- Daily Active People 3.64B +3% YoY
- Ad Impressions +10% YoY
- Average Price Per Ad +14% YoY
- Operating Cash Flow $32.8B
- FY26 CapEx Guidance $135B-$145B

Meta announced plans for an effective 2-for-1 stock split in January 2027. Rather than simply doubling existing shares, Meta will issue one new publicly traded, non-voting Class C share for every existing Class A or Class B share. This means shareholders will receive an additional share without changing their voting power.

This also means Meta will likely do an equity raise, but if they can continue putting up numbers like this, the street will have to digest it.

Mark Zuckerberg:

"We hit major milestones this quarter toward delivering personal superintelligence for everyone - including launching Muse and Muse Wonder, our first frontier model. Our investments are paying off, the core business is strong, and we're seeing velocity across the board."

item.dc:creator: @FinanceLancelot
item.description:
BREAKING: The OCC has passed the final rule of the Genius Act, paving the way for its implementation.
The final rule establishes a requirement for payment stablecoins and foreign payment stablecoin issuers under the OCC’s jurisdiction.
Congressional voting on the Clarity Act in January 2027 will define when digital assets are commodities versus securities, splitting oversight between the SEC and CFTC.
item.content:encoded:
BREAKING: The OCC has passed the final rule of the Genius Act, paving the way for its implementation.

The final rule establishes a requirement for payment stablecoins and foreign payment stablecoin issuers under the OCC’s jurisdiction.

Congressional voting on the Clarity Act in January 2027 will define when digital assets are commodities versus securities, splitting oversight between the SEC and CFTC.

item.title: @amitisinvesting: so $SPCX obviously blew the doors out with those earnings especially if Elon gets anywhere close to...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
so $SPCX obviously blew the doors out with those earnings
especially if Elon gets anywhere close to his goal of bringing 20GW online by next year
the question now seems to be what this means for every other neocloud
SpaceX is up today, the rest are flat to red.
On one hand, $SPCX proved how important the neocloud business model is and how much demand is out there.
On the other hand, $SPCX was so good that now people are doubting the ability for other neoclouds to easily finance their operations, how quickly those companies can bring compute online compared to Elon, and how much debt/dilution SpaceX themselves will have to take on to finance that buildout which then begs the question around how much dilution the smaller players will have to take on. SpaceX is also profitable whereas the others are years from profitability.
My take is more that $SPCX has validated the entire concept of neoclouds which obviously have been under stress given the $CRWV bonds getting hit over the past two weeks, but the earnings were also so good that there might be more questions now about how well the others can execute.
The broader theme seemed to be legitimized from those earnings: the compute constraints exist and have not eased up in any meaningful way.

item.title: @amitisinvesting: I have been psychologically short $NFLX for years and believe this year has vindicated that psychol...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
I have been psychologically short $NFLX for years and believe this year has vindicated that psychological short.
Unfortunately I was way too much of a chicken to actually short/buy puts 😂
In all seriousness, my bear case has always been that they cannot keep up content spend to justify their growth without massive hits. The massive hits have faded away which has significantly hurt the type of subscriber/adgrowth needed for the stock to expand from its premium multiple.
YouTube’s algorithm was another bear case. How does Netflix compete with a creator economy that is growing rapidly without spending even more money? The move to buy Warner Bros, live sports, podcasting…all of it was to hide that they just don’t have the massive hits needed to keep growing.
HOWEVER…at some point, the company becomes too cheap. Valuation is 5 year low and they are buying back a ton of stock. I genuinely don’t see how they get back to massive growth again without a MAJOR hit like Squid Games…all the ads/NFL/videogames/buybacks in the world won’t get the street excited without hits.
But I wonder if the margin of safety has finally gotten to the point where their most is being meaningfully discounted (I do think they have a large moat with huge barriers to entry) and if the stock price is officially reflecting that.
Are you buying the dip?
$NFLX -5%

item.title: @amitisinvesting: A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY. Here's a full recap: 1. SpaceX $SPCX reported a...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY.
Here's a full recap:
1. SpaceX $SPCX reported a massive Q3 2026, with revenue surging 161% YoY to $14.6B, while EPS reached $0.35 and net income totaled $4.4B. Adjusted EBITDA jumped 306% YoY to $8.8B, with operating cash flow of $13.1B and capital expenditures of $19.6B, highlighting the scale of the company's infrastructure investments. By segment, Space revenue grew 6% to $1.8B, Connectivity revenue increased 69% to $5.2B, and Space Intelligence (SI) revenue skyrocketed 830% to $7.6B, becoming the company's largest revenue contributor. Elon Musk also outlined aggressive expansion plans for AI compute, saying SpaceX could potentially have 20 GW of SI capacity online by the end of 2027, although he acknowledged that outcome is unlikely. Musk added that he would be surprised if SpaceX deployed less than 13 GW of compute capacity by the end of next year, underscoring the company's ambitions in large-scale AI infrastructure.
2. Anthropic’s draft IPO prospectus reportedly reveals explosive growth alongside unprecedented AI infrastructure commitments, with H1 2026 revenue surging nearly 15x YoY to $16.3B, up from $1.1B, while computing expenses climbed to nearly $9B. The company recorded an $80.7B net loss, although approximately $72B came from accounting adjustments tied to convertible notes and other financing instruments rather than direct operating expenses. Anthropic has reportedly committed roughly $450B to long-term cloud contracts, plus more than $160B for Google-designed AI chips through Broadcom $AVGO, with additional negotiations potentially pushing total computing commitments toward $750B. Major suppliers include Google $GOOGL ($111B), Amazon $AMZN ($110B), Microsoft $MSFT ($31B), and Nscale and Lambda (up to $86B), while the prospectus also highlights risks around customer concentration, power availability, infrastructure execution, and AI-related liability. Anthropic is reportedly preparing for a potential IPO at a valuation approaching $2T, underscoring the extraordinary scale of both the revenue opportunity and capital requirements facing frontier AI developers.
3. Supermicro $SMCI significantly raised its preliminary Q1 FY2027 revenue guidance to $18.5B–$19.5B, up from its previous outlook of $14.5B–$15.5B, representing a 27% increase at the midpoint. The company attributed the stronger outlook to accelerating demand for AI infrastructure platforms, reflecting continued investment in next-generation data center systems. Supermicro also raised its expected gross margin to 12.0%–12.5%, up from 10.4%–10.8%, citing a more favorable customer and product mix. The combination of sharply higher revenue expectations and improving margins suggests stronger operating leverage as demand for AI computing infrastructure continues to expand.
4. Citadel founder Ken Griffin warned that investors are “almost certainly” in an AI bubble, raising concerns about the enormous amounts of capital being deployed into artificial intelligence without corresponding evidence of widespread productivity gains. Griffin pointed to the scale of AI infrastructure commitments, with Anthropic reportedly considering as much as $750B in future computing expenditures, as investors increasingly question whether AI companies can generate sufficient returns to justify their spending. Despite his concerns about elevated valuations, aggressive capital expenditures, and speculative enthusiasm, Griffin remains bullish on AI’s long-term transformative potential, distinguishing between the technology’s eventual economic impact and the possibility that investors are paying too much for that growth today.
5. The top 10 most active options today by contracts traded were $NVDA with 2.3M contracts, $AAPL with 1.0M contracts, $SPCX with 992K contracts, $NFLX with 876K contracts, $MU with 850K contracts, $TSLA with 843K contracts, $AMZN with 824K contracts, $CRWV with 785K contracts, $INTC with 621K contracts, and $AMD with 480K contracts.
6. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said U.S.–Iran negotiations remain ongoing through mediators including Pakistan and Qatar, but accused Washington of complicating diplomatic progress by introducing new conditions to a previously proposed seven-day agreement. According to Araghchi, the U.S. initially accepted Iran’s terms before seeking additional clauses, while Tehran’s proposal called for the Strait of Hormuz to fully reopen on day six of the arrangement. Araghchi emphasized that Iran remains open to negotiations if Washington honors previously discussed understandings, despite what he described as deep distrust between the two countries. He declined to publicly detail the additional U.S. demands, leaving the outcome of the negotiations uncertain as both sides continue working through intermediaries.
7. U.S. pending home sales plunged 7.3% in September, falling to their lowest level on record in data going back to 2001. The decline was particularly severe in the West, where pending sales dropped 9.2%, while the South, the nation's largest home-selling region, recorded an 8.2% contraction. The sharp deterioration highlights the continued paralysis in the U.S. housing market, as elevated mortgage rates, affordability challenges, and economic uncertainty weigh on homebuyer demand.
8. Amazon $AMZN announced plans to invest more than €16B ($18B) in Germany during 2027, expanding its AI infrastructure, AWS cloud operations, logistics network, and robotics capabilities. The investment includes €4.8B for AWS, supporting expansion of its Frankfurt cloud region, alongside a second AI and robotics research lab in Berlin. Amazon also plans to expand its Leo satellite broadband network through 24 Arianespace launches, while new logistics projects are expected to create more than 3,000 jobs. The commitment brings Amazon's cumulative investment in Germany to more than €100B since 2010, reinforcing the country's importance as a European hub for AI infrastructure, cloud computing, and advanced logistics.
9. Meta $META has completed the first phase of its gigawatt-scale Prometheus AI supercluster in Ohio, connecting hundreds of thousands of NVIDIA $NVDA GPUs across multiple buildings into a single massive AI training system, with plans to eventually scale to 1 million GPUs. The infrastructure combines NVIDIA GB200 and GB300 NVL72 platforms and was used to train Meta's latest Muse Wonder AI models. Meta said extensive engineering work with NVIDIA on hardware reliability, networking, and firmware has reduced training interruptions by 99% from their peak, enabling more than 85% productive training time during pretraining and over 90% during reinforcement learning. The company plans to expand Prometheus further using NVIDIA's next-generation Vera Rubin systems, highlighting the enormous infrastructure requirements behind the development of frontier AI models.
10. Netflix $NFLX reported Q3 2026 revenue of $12.87B, in line with expectations and up 12% YoY, while EPS of $0.87 beat the $0.82 estimate, rising 49% YoY. Operating income surged 37% to $4.46B, exceeding expectations, with operating margins expanding 640 basis points to 34.6%, reflecting strong profitability despite moderating revenue growth. However, the biggest disappointment came from guidance, with Netflix lowering its FY2026 free cash flow outlook to $12B from $12.5B and reducing its advertising revenue forecast to approximately $2.7B from $3B, while guiding Q4 revenue of $13.44B and EPS of $0.67, both below consensus. Regional growth remained positive, led by Latin America (+17%), while UCAN and EMEA each grew 11% and APAC increased 12%. Netflix also generated $2.88B in quarterly free cash flow, repurchased $4.8B in shares, and announced plans to expand its advertising tier into 15 additional countries in 2027, highlighting continued investment in monetization despite a softer near-term outlook.
11. Citadel Securities strategist Scott Rubner believes AI stocks could resume outperforming after the U.S. midterm elections, as institutional investors wait for political uncertainty to clear before increasing exposure, according to Bloomberg. Rubner said clients remain interested in the AI trade but are reluctant to deploy additional capital ahead of a major political event, with some telling him they are “happy to buy higher, but not buy now into a major political event.” The comments suggest that some investors are delaying purchases rather than abandoning their bullish outlook on AI, potentially creating renewed demand for technology stocks once the elections are over.
12. Amazon $AMZN is reportedly accelerating purchases of NVIDIA $NVDA AI server racks, but power shortages and data center deployment delays are leaving some expensive equipment idle before it can generate revenue. Internal AWS projections reportedly showed approximately $5B in GB300 rack deliveries in August, followed by roughly $3B per month, although these figures represent projected deliveries rather than confirmed idle inventory. Amazon has also introduced an Early Rack Receipt program that allows AWS to take ownership and pay for AI hardware before it reaches data centers, securing scarce GPU supply but accelerating cash outflows. The challenges come as Amazon expects approximately $220B in capital expenditures during 2026, with free cash flow turning negative last quarter for the first time since 2023. Amazon maintains that staging equipment near data centers is standard practice and disputes claims of broader deployment-planning problems, highlighting the growing tension between rapid AI infrastructure investment and the power capacity needed to monetize it.
WALL STREET IS THE GREATEST SHOW ON EARTH.

item.description:
Here is some advice for the ones who wish to grow a following or build a brand:
Have value and stick to it.
Allow others to hold different views.
Expect jealousy from lesser talent.
Only answer slander - trolls are traffic.
Don't be afraid to recognize others.
Avoid drama marketing. It is draining.
If you have a product, service or a viewpoint worth listening to... People will notice and word of mouth will do the rest.
Impatience communicates novice poverty driven motives.
Slow is smooth, smooth is fast.

item.title: @I_Am_The_ICT: It never ceases to surprise me when people reply with the cringe responses they reach for. I'm sinc...
item.dc:creator: @I_Am_The_ICT
item.description:
It never ceases to surprise me when people reply with the cringe responses they reach for.
I'm sincerely asking here... does your day suck that much?
If someone does well - acknowledgement is hated.
If a female student kicks major ass and carries proof - I'm simping.
If I include our community in a collective manner - it is cultish.
If I call a specific price run and it goes there - it was another random guess.
Miserable mindsets get muted.
I don't have time for whiners... just winners.

item.title: @FinanceLancelot: SpaceX $SPCX shocked the market today by announcing they will be releasing their Q3 earnings report...
item.dc:creator: @FinanceLancelot
item.description:
SpaceX $SPCX shocked the market today by announcing they will be releasing their Q3 earnings report tomorrow.
This is extremely unusual with no notice.
Analysts expected a report in around November 3, 5, or 17, consistent with the gap after the August 4 Q2 report.
So why are they doing this?
Reports indicate SpaceX is seeking around $40 billion of new funding to buy $NVDA chips ($10 billion in loans + ~$30 billion in investment-grade debt).
But the real reason is likely this...
28% SpaceX share unlock is triggered solely by the public release of SpaceX’s Q3 2026 results.
So not only are we going to see 28% of shares hitting the market on October 22nd, but on Sunday October 25th an additional 7% of shares get unlocked as well.
Why is Elon rushing to unlock these insider shares?
Does he know a market crash is coming? 🤔
