item.title: @amitisinvesting: A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY. Here's a full recap: 1. Amazon $AMZN posted its...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY.
Here's a full recap:
1. Amazon $AMZN posted its best trading day since August, supported by a bullish Morgan Stanley outlook and a major development in its custom AI chip strategy. Morgan Stanley named Amazon its top pick, setting a $350 price target that implies approximately 40% upside, while raising its AWS growth forecasts to 47% and 42% YoY for 2027 and 2028, respectively. Separately, Amazon unveiled TorchNeuron, a new software tool that allows developers to run existing PyTorch AI workloads on Trainium2 and Trainium3 chips with minimal code changes. The development could help reduce one of the biggest barriers to adopting Amazon's custom silicon and strengthen its competitive position against NVIDIA $NVDA, whose CUDA software ecosystem has historically been a major advantage in the AI infrastructure market.
2. ARK Invest updated its 2031 Tesla $TSLA valuation model, projecting a $4,400 base-case share price, representing approximately 12x upside from current levels. The firm expects robotaxis to account for roughly 80% of Tesla’s enterprise value by 2031, forecasting a fleet of 8.1M autonomous vehicles generating $753B in annual ride-hailing revenue, with operating costs potentially 40% below Waymo’s. ARK also sees Optimus humanoid robots emerging as Tesla’s second major growth engine, projecting approximately 1M robots sold externally and $212B in annual revenue by 2031, supported by an estimated $26T addressable robotics market. To support these ambitions, ARK expects Tesla to invest approximately $225B cumulatively in AI infrastructure through 2031, underscoring how heavily its valuation thesis depends on the successful commercialization and scaling of autonomous driving and robotics.
3. Microsoft $MSFT has reportedly withdrawn from a major UK data center agreement with British neocloud provider Nscale, according to The Telegraph, dealing a setback to the startup ahead of its planned $3B IPO. The proposed facility in Loughton, Essex, has faced repeated delays, with authorities reportedly not expecting sufficient power availability until the 2030s. Anthropic is also reportedly in talks to purchase $45B worth of AI computing capacity from Nscale, the NVIDIA-backed data center developer, according to Bloomberg.
4. A potential breakthrough agreement between the United States and Iran could be announced as early as this week, according to Al-Araby Al-Jadeed, citing sources familiar with ongoing mediation efforts. Negotiators are reportedly working to narrow remaining differences and secure mutual concessions aimed at preventing a renewed military escalation between Washington and Tehran. While the reported progress could represent a significant diplomatic development amid heightened tensions in the Middle East, no agreement has been officially confirmed, and negotiations remain ongoing.
5. Anthropic announced the creation of the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, pledging an initial 5% of company equity to support charitable initiatives and address the broader societal impacts of AI, including its effects on employment. Subject to shareholder approval, the company’s board may contribute an additional 2% of shares for every 50% increase in valuation above an undisclosed baseline. Elon Musk also said that next year, he will give every American child one share of $SPCX, which would be worth $10.5B at today's prices. He says this will be the first of many times he gives shares to the public.
6. JPMorgan says the latest October selloff in Korean semiconductor and memory stocks looks materially different from the July correction, with several factors potentially limiting a rebound. Unlike July, retail investors have shown little appetite to buy the dip, while short interest across Korean equities, U.S. memory stocks, semiconductor ETFs such as $SMH, and broader indexes like $SPY remains relatively low. JPM also warned that leveraged ETF exposure has increased since late July, making the market more vulnerable to further selling pressure. Compounding the risks, a combined $40B share buyback program from South Korea's two largest memory manufacturers was accelerated to finish in mid-October, removing a significant source of buying support that helped stabilize the market in recent months.
7. Russian President Vladimir Putin has reportedly proposed a three-way meeting with President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping to negotiate a potential end to the war in Ukraine, according to the Wall Street Journal. Putin reportedly raised the proposal during an October 9 phone call with Trump, with the meeting potentially taking place next month. The proposed summit would bring together the leaders of Russia, the United States, and China in an effort to explore a diplomatic resolution to the conflict, although no meeting or peace agreement has been confirmed.
8. South Korean AI infrastructure company Elice plunged approximately 30% on its stock market debut, despite raising $151M at a $750M valuation in an IPO that was reportedly 400x oversubscribed by retail investors. Elice specializes in GPU cloud rentals and the software infrastructure used to manage AI computing workloads, making its listing a notable test of investor appetite for AI infrastructure companies. The sharp decline came amid a broader selloff in South Korean equities, with the KOSPI falling 4.2% to below its July lows, while Samsung Electronics declined 3% and SK Hynix dropped 6%. If the decline holds through the close, Elice could record the worst IPO debut in South Korean market history, highlighting the growing disconnect between strong investor demand for AI-related offerings and increasingly volatile public market valuations.
9. S&P 500 $SPY put option trading volume surged to a record $3.3T in notional value on Friday, marking an extraordinary increase in downside positioning and hedging activity. The dollar value of S&P 500 puts traded was approximately 330% above the 2024 daily average, compared with typical daily volumes of just $100B–$500B before the 2020 pandemic. Meanwhile, total CBOE put option volume reached 9.6M contracts, the fourth-highest daily reading since 2015. The surge highlights an unprecedented level of activity in downside protection as investors navigate elevated market uncertainty, although record put volume does not necessarily indicate outright bearish positioning, since options are also used for hedging and complex trading strategies.
10. Morgan Stanley strategist Michael Wilson believes the three-month U.S. equity correction may be approaching its final stages, urging investors to prepare for potential buying opportunities rather than assume the broader bull market is ending. Since mid-August, high-quality stocks have gained roughly 6%, while the equal-weight S&P 500 has declined nearly 4% and cyclical stocks have fallen almost 10%, highlighting the growing divergence beneath the index. He believes the correction reflects a transition toward a more selective, mid-cycle market rather than the end of the economic expansion, with investors potentially getting an opportunity to buy the dip as the adjustment concludes.
11. The top 10 most active options today by contracts traded were $NVDA with 3.3M contracts, $TSLA with 2.8M contracts, $AMZN with 1.5M contracts, $AAPL with 1.5M contracts, $MU with 1.4M contracts, $SPCX with 1.0M contracts, $INTC with 816K contracts, $CRWV with 778K contracts, $META with 754K contracts, and $AMD with 743K contracts.
12. JPMorgan significantly raised its AI data center capital expenditure forecasts, now expecting spending to grow 85% YoY in 2026, up from 80%, and 70% in 2027, up from its previous 50% estimate. The firm projects more than $270B in incremental data center spending in 2026 and another record increase of $400B+ in 2027, with total spending across major U.S. hyperscalers and other operators approaching $800B in 2026 and $1.5T in 2027. JPM highlighted Credo $CRDO, Lumentum $LITE, Coherent $COHR, Amphenol $APH, Arista $ANET, Celestica $CLS, Ciena $CIEN, Corning $GLW, and Fabrinet $FN as key beneficiaries of the accelerating infrastructure buildout.

item.title: @FinanceLancelot: The talking heads on CNBC are telling everyone to pile back into memory stocks because "They're che...
item.dc:creator: @FinanceLancelot
item.description:
The talking heads on CNBC are telling everyone to pile back into memory stocks because "They're cheap compared to earnings"...
What they aren't telling you is P/E is totally irrelevant for memory stocks.
Every single memory cycle has rolled over when gross margins peak.
During Micron's $MU last earnings call, their guidance warned us that gross margins will be lower next Q.
The other thing they aren't telling you is memory is notoriously a boom and bust industry.
A period of record earnings is always followed by a bust, because companies double and triple order memory chips.
When the prices begin to fall, their customers cancel all of those orders and pay a small fee.
Also, memory fabs have massive fixed costs. When prices begin to fall they can't simply stop production. They must keep producing regardless of price, which causes a price spiral into a memory glut.
At least @stephenLweiss was warning people what's coming with the memory bust. He also said he's sold a lot of his AI holdings.
He's right, the memory companies always say the same thing at the top... every... single... time.

item.title: @FinanceLancelot: GameStop $GME is finally rolling over to return to the giant 2021 wedge. This was 1 week later than...
item.dc:creator: @FinanceLancelot
item.description:
GameStop $GME is finally rolling over to return to the giant 2021 wedge.
This was 1 week later than the 2020 pattern, but it's still following the script pretty closely.
Ryan Cohen only owns 9.1% of shares, so he still needs 7 weeks to get up to the 9.98% that he held in September 2020.
The reason he doesn't break 10% is anyone who owns more than 10% of a registered class of a company's equity securities is classified as a "ten percent beneficial owner" (an insider).
They're subject to strict short-swing profit rules (Section 16b), where any profits realized from purchases and sales can potentially be disgorged to the company.

item.title: @amitisinvesting: AMAZON HAS ITS BEST DAY SINCE AUGUST: - Morgan Stanley named Amazon their topic pick, sees 40% upsi...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
AMAZON HAS ITS BEST DAY SINCE AUGUST:
- Morgan Stanley named Amazon their topic pick, sees 40% upside with a PT to $350
- Amazon announced TorchNeuron, a new software tool designed to make it easier for developers to run existing PyTorch AI workloads on its Trainium2 and Trainium3 chips with minimal code changes, reducing a major barrier to adoption and helping Amazon compete with Nvidia $NVDA, whose CUDA software ecosystem has historically been a key competitive advantage.
- AWS projections increased to 47% and 42% YoY growth through 2027-2028 by Morgan Stanley
Amazon has underperformed the Nasdaq $QQQ over the past 5 years, with the Nasdaq up 94% and Amazon up 50%.
It feels like the consensus view is that 2027 will be the year of Amazon...but that consensus view has also been similar over the past 2 years.
If 2027 is the year for Amazon, it would be based on AWS + Trainium inflecting along with inflows in general beginning to rotate from Semis to Mag 7.
$AMZN +5%

item.title: @amitisinvesting: The question is not if we will have a bear market, the question is if this administration can affor...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
The question is not if we will have a bear market, the question is if this administration can afford to let us have a bear market.
- AI Capex is 50% of GDP. If it stops or slows down, GDP growth goes down the drain. No GDP growth = recession. Mainstreet gets hit the worst as the labor market will collapse.
- 90% of consumer spending is done by the top 10%. They are levered against their assets that allow them to keep spending because their stocks keep going up. Stocks go down? Goodbye to consumer spending as we enter an actual recession given normal consumers already are borrowing from credit cards to pay for everything.
- Social security will be wrecked over the coming 10 years. Why do you think we got the Trump Accounts? Because the administration believes in financial literacy? No, they need a replacement and having kids compound in the stock market to basically build their retirement account from birth could replace social security. That means stocks have to go up for those accounts to be worth anything and actually compound. Most 401Ks in this country are basically seen as retirement accounts. If the admin lets the market crash, people will not be able to afford retirement when social security benefits get cut into 2032.
- We are $40T in debt. Bond yields continue to go higher which means the interest expense on our debt is approaching a significant part of our overall spending. The literal only way to solve this is cut spending or grow. Repubs or Dems will not cut spending…so growth is the only answer. If the market crashes, the chances of sustained growth in the greatest tech buildout we have ever seen will be impossible and ultimately make our debt situation even worse. We have to grow.
Not saying we can’t get into some horrible bear market, but given how levered the entire economy is to AI, which is basically the entire stock market, I do think this admin will try very hard to make sure we don’t have some horrible, ugly crash. If they let it happen, everything goes down the drain and the difference between now and dotcom is that demand for GPUs is very real (no oversupply) and the difference between now and 2008 is that the potential credit issue is not in housing and banks, it’s within GPUs and there is so much demand that the hyperscalers + Nvidia + the admin could come in to make sure things don’t get as bad as then.
Maybe we could have some epic crash, but this administration really cannot afford to let that happen.

item.title: @FinanceLancelot: Dow Jones / VIX has broken the upward trend. If markets are topped out and preparing for a major vo...
item.dc:creator: @FinanceLancelot
item.description:
Dow Jones / VIX has broken the upward trend.
If markets are topped out and preparing for a major volatility event, usually what we see here is a bounce or two before they finally let go.
Volmageddon in Feb 5th, 2018 has a brief 1 week bounce before the entire market let go.
In January 2020, the market had a small flash crash below trend then rallied for 4 weeks, which drew everyone right back into the market.
While October 2018 it broke trend, then bounced until markets crashed at the end of the year and 2019.
We just don't know which scenario we're in.

from October 2018 until the end of the year we saw a bounce before it finally rolled over though.
During the economic slowdown of 2022 it was the same, but what saved markets was the Biden administration rolling all of the debt to the short end of the yield curve.
That allowed the Biden administration to spend like a drunken Saylor and save the economy through government spending.
This time however, Trump won't have that option. The entire global bond market is tapped out of cash.
Nobody can find the money to save the economy this time.

dip has been bought.
$7500 in my solo 401k...idea here was to buy semis that are really getting hurt or names that I don't mind holding for a decade and are near their 52-week lows
semis getting hurt bad: $SMCI $TSM $AVGO $NBIS
out of these 4, SMCI is the one I like the least but it's also touching the 3month low and DELL has taken enough of a beating for SMCI to get a rebound if there is any bounce within server racks
the two large cap semis like $TSM and $AVGO I can see myself holding for a very long time as they are relatively safe and have real moats, $NBIS should bounce here but maybe more neocloud fears hurt it...the diversification of their business is some hedge to the pure GPU licensing business
the other 3 $TSLA $RKLB $SOFI i can imagine holding for a long time and 40% drawdowns feel like enough pain but I believe they all 3 will be fine in the long term, Tesla's short term catalyst is the roadster event, Rocketlab is down aggressively from $150 so I see that being a spot where some buyers step in even with the neutron delays, and $SOFI should benefit if yields come down but obviously rate hikes are an issue for them and every bank
didn't do much in my regular brokerage...bought most of the SaaS dips months ago with $PLTR $ZETA $SHOP $RDDT and have not been playing semis outside of $NVDA and $AVGO really...still holding the $DRAM $INTC and $BE position I bought in August which are either slightly up/flat since then
maybe we are headed another leg lower before the midterms but time will tell now 🤷‍♂️

item.title: @amitisinvesting: if you're wondering why the 10-year is down today even though CPI had a horrible print...which shou...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
if you're wondering why the 10-year is down today even though CPI had a horrible print...which should be causing yields to go up because that means we have a higher chance of a rate hike due to more inflation...
i *think* it's because the bond market wants to see the stock market go down.
and not just stocks, but AI/semi/capex stocks in particular.
the theory i've had over the past couple of weeks is that as we see more issuance of corporate debt in order to fuel capex...that is obviously competing with the long end of the curve for US treasuries
i mean, one can even argue that bond yields we're going to go up regardless of the oil issues because those yields simply couldn't stay at 4% if meta/google/amzn/msft were offering 6-7% on their corporate debt
so the obvious answer now could be for there to be LESS competition with the US 10-year...but the only way for that to happen is for their to be lower-yielding debt from the hyperscalers that are issuing bonds to fuel their capex spend
well...the only way that happens is if the capex stops, slows down, or the cost to build these datacenters drop so that the borrowing costs drop
which is why we have seen yields RISE every day over the past few weeks when semis go up and we are seeing them go down when semis go down...it's like the credit market is saying "we will only buy bonds if you guys stop buying semis"
this doesn't mean that stocks writ-large have to go down, but it does mean that the credit markets are asking for something to break in the equity markets and its like they want semis to be the main culprit. if semis keep going to the moon, cool, but then so will yields and then maybe a 6% 10-year is what breaks everything?
not sure if this theory is right but the objectively true part is the competition between US corp debt and treasuries, if all that corp debt is going to buy semis then when semis go down, it makes sense for treasuries to go up
the easiest way to get SOME relief here is for Trump to end the war so gas/energy comes down and puts relief on inflation...but today's CPI showed the opposite and yields STILL went down because semis got hit
it's a very, very weird time to understand how the bond market is navigating the AI trade

well...the only way that happens is if the capex stops, slows down, or the cost to build these datacenters drop so that the borrowing costs drop

item.title: @amitisinvesting: A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY. Here's a full recap: 1. Q3 2026 earnings season...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY.
Here's a full recap:
1. Q3 2026 earnings season got underway with reports from JPMorgan $JPM, Goldman Sachs $GS, Citigroup $C, and Wells Fargo $WFC, delivering a mixed but generally resilient picture for the banking sector. Goldman Sachs led the group with a standout quarter, posting its second-best revenue quarter ever as equities trading surged 72%, while Citigroup reported its strongest third quarter in a decade, driven by strength in services, wealth management, and equities. JPMorgan delivered a rare earnings miss despite raising its 2026 net interest income outlook, and Wells Fargo beat on earnings but missed on revenue. Across the sector, banks continued to describe the U.S. consumer as resilient, highlighted ongoing AI-driven corporate investment, raised or maintained optimistic net interest income expectations, and pointed to strong equity trading activity, while cautioning that sticky inflation, higher-for-longer interest rates, elevated valuations, and geopolitical risks remain key challenges heading into 2027.
2. Bank of America said 10-year U.S. Treasury yields may need to approach 6% before investors meaningfully rotate out of stocks and into bonds, according to its latest Global Fund Manager Survey. The survey found 76% of respondents expect the Fed to leave rates unchanged in October, while technology allocations climbed to their highest level since August 2020 and long semiconductors remained the market’s most crowded trade. At the same time, consumer discretionary exposure fell to its lowest level since July 2008, with investors increasing allocations to bonds, utilities, Japan, and the U.K. while trimming exposure to banks and U.S. equities. Bank of America said equity sentiment remains resilient overall, but a disorderly rise in bond yields and the potential for an AI bubble are now viewed as the biggest risks facing markets.
3. Paul Tudor Jones warned that 2027 could be “a very challenging year for the market,” saying current conditions remind him “exactly like 1999.” He argued the market could continue performing well in the short term but believes long-term risks are building, noting that many investors have not experienced a similar cycle before. Jones also said he expects to remain short throughout 2027, arguing that valuations offer little value and drawing parallels to the 1998–2002 period, when heavy IPO issuance and insider share unlocks continually added supply to the market, creating what he described as one of the easiest environments to maintain short positions.
4. Apple $AAPL unveiled HomeView, its first dedicated smart home hub, at today’s “Welcome Home” event, marking the company’s biggest smart home expansion since HomeKit. The $299 device features a 7-inch Liquid Retina display, Siri AI, Face ID support for up to 6 users, FaceTime, Matter and Thread compatibility, and centralized control for cameras, locks, lights, thermostats, and other smart home devices, with pre-orders open now and shipments. Apple also introduced the HomePod mini 2 ($149), a new Apple TV 4K ($299), and the Apple Home Collection of smart home accessories, including cameras, a video doorbell, smart locks, thermostats, and sensors, developed with LG and Schneider Electric. The announcements represent Apple’s most aggressive push yet into the connected home, positioning the company to compete more directly with Amazon Echo and Google Nest while emphasizing privacy, on-device intelligence, and deep ecosystem integration.
5. Oracle $ORCL is urging federal regulators to expedite approval of the Green Chile natural gas pipeline, arguing the project is critical to keeping construction of its massive Project Jupiter AI data center in New Mexico on schedule. In a letter to FERC, Oracle SVP Josh Pitcock said further delays could jeopardize the project’s timeline, along with the associated jobs, economic activity, and community benefits. The Energy Transfer-owned pipeline is expected to supply roughly 400 million cubic feet of natural gas per day to Bloom Energy fuel cells powering Project Jupiter, but commissioning has slipped to February 2027 from the previously expected August 15 start date.
6. OpenAI said it discovered a sophisticated recording device inside one of its offices after an employee allegedly installed it several days earlier. The company said the employee has been terminated and the matter has been referred to the FBI. According to OpenAI, there is no evidence that the individual improperly accessed or exfiltrated model weights, source code, or customer data. The incident highlights the growing importance of physical and operational security as AI companies safeguard increasingly valuable intellectual property.
7. NVIDIA $NVDA CEO Jensen Huang said the company will announce an additional $2B investment in Europe next week, bringing NVIDIA's regional investment to roughly $10B over the past year. Huang, who is scheduled to visit London and Berlin, also announced new investments in four French AI startups: Doctolib, Genesis AI, Pigment, and Entalpic. Addressing concerns over AI safety and data center energy consumption, Huang argued that AI can be developed safely while driving economic growth, opposed slowing AI development, and said open-source models could help Europe narrow the AI gap with the U.S. by enabling language- and industry-specific customization. He urged Europe to accelerate its AI investment and innovation efforts as global competition intensifies.
8. The top 10 most active options today by contracts traded were $NVDA with 1.7M contracts, $AAPL with 1.2M contracts, $MU with 1.0M contracts, $META with 975K contracts, $SPCX with 971K contracts, $TSLA with 911K contracts, $INTC with 792K contracts, $MSFT with 507K contracts, $AMZN with 496K contracts, and $AMD with 489K contracts.
9. The latest ADP National Employment Report showed U.S. private employers added an average of 24,750 jobs per week over the four weeks ending September 26, down from a 25,250 weekly average previously and marking the end of five consecutive weeks of improving hiring. The latest reading represents a 2% decline in weekly job creation, although hiring remains well above the 8,250 weekly average recorded in late July. The softer hiring trend could point to a gradually cooling labor market, potentially easing wage pressures and inflation over time. Investors will now look to upcoming employment reports for confirmation of whether the slowdown is becoming more broad-based and what it could mean for future Federal Reserve policy.
10. Bank of America $BAC has been hit with $1.2B in penalties by the U.S. Treasury Department over alleged violations of anti-money laundering and sanctions laws, marking the third-largest Treasury enforcement action of its kind. BofA said they will take a 17C EPS hit on earnings in Q3 as this is not a tax deductible expense.
11. Netflix $NFLX has secured the exclusive broadcast rights to the 2030 FIFA Men’s World Cup in Spain and Andorra, covering all 104 matches, with financial terms undisclosed. The agreement significantly expands Netflix’s live sports portfolio, which already includes NFL games and the rights to the next two FIFA Women’s World Cups. Investors welcomed the announcement, with Netflix shares rising about 1% in premarket trading. The deal strengthens Netflix’s push into premium live sports as it continues broadening its content strategy beyond traditional streaming.
12. JPMorgan says a small group of 42 AI-related companies is driving the vast majority of corporate growth, accounting for roughly 60–80% of S&P 500 earnings growth. At the same time, market breadth has continued to deteriorate, with about 60% of S&P 500 stocks now trading at least 20% below their all-time highs. JPM also noted that only 30% of stocks have outperformed the S&P 500, the lowest participation rate since 1991, highlighting the increasingly concentrated nature of the current bull market.
WALL STREET IS THE GREATEST SHOW ON EARTH.

2. Bank of America said 10-year U.S. Treasury yields may need to approach 6% before investors meaningfully rotate out of stocks and into bonds, according to its latest Global Fund Manager Survey. The survey found 76% of respondents expect the Fed to leave rates unchanged in October, while technology allocations climbed to their highest level since August 2020 and long semiconductors remained the market’s most crowded trade. At the same time, consumer discretionary exposure fell to its lowest level since July 2008, with investors increasing allocations to bonds, utilities, Japan, and the U.K. while trimming exposure to banks and U.S. equities. Bank of America said equity sentiment remains resilient overall, but a disorderly rise in bond yields and the potential for an AI bubble are now viewed as the biggest risks facing markets.

3. Paul Tudor Jones warned that 2027 could be “a very challenging year for the market,” saying current conditions remind him “exactly like 1999.” He argued the market could continue performing well in the short term but believes long-term risks are building, noting that many investors have not experienced a similar cycle before. Jones also said he expects to remain short throughout 2027, arguing that valuations offer little value and drawing parallels to the 1998–2002 period, when heavy IPO issuance and insider share unlocks continually added supply to the market, creating what he described as one of the easiest environments to maintain short positions.

4. Apple $AAPL unveiled HomeView, its first dedicated smart home hub, at today’s “Welcome Home” event, marking the company’s biggest smart home expansion since HomeKit. The $299 device features a 7-inch Liquid Retina display, Siri AI, Face ID support for up to 6 users, FaceTime, Matter and Thread compatibility, and centralized control for cameras, locks, lights, thermostats, and other smart home devices, with pre-orders open now and shipments. Apple also introduced the HomePod mini 2 ($149), a new Apple TV 4K ($299), and the Apple Home Collection of smart home accessories, including cameras, a video doorbell, smart locks, thermostats, and sensors, developed with LG and Schneider Electric. The announcements represent Apple’s most aggressive push yet into the connected home, positioning the company to compete more directly with Amazon Echo and Google Nest while emphasizing privacy, on-device intelligence, and deep ecosystem integration.

5. Oracle $ORCL is urging federal regulators to expedite approval of the Green Chile natural gas pipeline, arguing the project is critical to keeping construction of its massive Project Jupiter AI data center in New Mexico on schedule. In a letter to FERC, Oracle SVP Josh Pitcock said further delays could jeopardize the project’s timeline, along with the associated jobs, economic activity, and community benefits. The Energy Transfer-owned pipeline is expected to supply roughly 400 million cubic feet of natural gas per day to Bloom Energy fuel cells powering Project Jupiter, but commissioning has slipped to February 2027 from the previously expected August 15 start date.

6. OpenAI said it discovered a sophisticated recording device inside one of its offices after an employee allegedly installed it several days earlier. The company said the employee has been terminated and the matter has been referred to the FBI. According to OpenAI, there is no evidence that the individual improperly accessed or exfiltrated model weights, source code, or customer data. The incident highlights the growing importance of physical and operational security as AI companies safeguard increasingly valuable intellectual property.

7. NVIDIA $NVDA CEO Jensen Huang said the company will announce an additional $2B investment in Europe next week, bringing NVIDIA's regional investment to roughly $10B over the past year. Huang, who is scheduled to visit London and Berlin, also announced new investments in four French AI startups: Doctolib, Genesis AI, Pigment, and Entalpic. Addressing concerns over AI safety and data center energy consumption, Huang argued that AI can be developed safely while driving economic growth, opposed slowing AI development, and said open-source models could help Europe narrow the AI gap with the U.S. by enabling language- and industry-specific customization. He urged Europe to accelerate its AI investment and innovation efforts as global competition intensifies.

8. The top 10 most active options today by contracts traded were $NVDA with 1.7M contracts, $AAPL with 1.2M contracts, $MU with 1.0M contracts, $META with 975K contracts, $SPCX with 971K contracts, $TSLA with 911K contracts, $INTC with 792K contracts, $MSFT with 507K contracts, $AMZN with 496K contracts, and $AMD with 489K contracts.

9. The latest ADP National Employment Report showed U.S. private employers added an average of 24,750 jobs per week over the four weeks ending September 26, down from a 25,250 weekly average previously and marking the end of five consecutive weeks of improving hiring. The latest reading represents a 2% decline in weekly job creation, although hiring remains well above the 8,250 weekly average recorded in late July. The softer hiring trend could point to a gradually cooling labor market, potentially easing wage pressures and inflation over time. Investors will now look to upcoming employment reports for confirmation of whether the slowdown is becoming more broad-based and what it could mean for future Federal Reserve policy.

10. Bank of America $BAC has been hit with $1.2B in penalties by the U.S. Treasury Department over alleged violations of anti-money laundering and sanctions laws, marking the third-largest Treasury enforcement action of its kind. BofA said they will take a 17C EPS hit on earnings in Q3 as this is not a tax deductible expense.

11. Netflix $NFLX has secured the exclusive broadcast rights to the 2030 FIFA Men’s World Cup in Spain and Andorra, covering all 104 matches, with financial terms undisclosed. The agreement significantly expands Netflix’s live sports portfolio, which already includes NFL games and the rights to the next two FIFA Women’s World Cups. Investors welcomed the announcement, with Netflix shares rising about 1% in premarket trading. The deal strengthens Netflix’s push into premium live sports as it continues broadening its content strategy beyond traditional streaming.

12. JPMorgan says a small group of 42 AI-related companies is driving the vast majority of corporate growth, accounting for roughly 60–80% of S&P 500 earnings growth. At the same time, market breadth has continued to deteriorate, with about 60% of S&P 500 stocks now trading at least 20% below their all-time highs. JPM also noted that only 30% of stocks have outperformed the S&P 500, the lowest participation rate since 1991, highlighting the increasingly concentrated nature of the current bull market.

WALL STREET IS THE GREATEST SHOW ON EARTH.

item.title: @FinanceLancelot: Jamie Dimon gave a stark warning to all governments this week when asked about 🇫🇷 France and pote...
item.dc:creator: @FinanceLancelot
item.description:
Jamie Dimon gave a stark warning to all governments this week when asked about 🇫🇷 France and potential contagion risk.
"It's a warning to governments. We can't borrow endlessly and spend endlessly."
What's interesting here is he went onto say that this government funding risk will actually feed into corporate debt and corporate credit spreads.
We're already seeing this in the AI bubble, as credit default swaps on AI hyper-scalers like Oracle $ORCL continue to blow out to the upside.
Remember, back in 2011 when the European Banking Crisis began is was largely a government funding issue in 🇬🇷 Greece and 🇮🇹 Italy.
What happened after that was forced austerity by the IMF and ECB, in order to curtail government spending to qualify for the bailout.
This rippled directly into the banking system, with a sudden corporate and private credit collapse, which had a dramatic impact on unemployment.
2 years later in 2013, youth unemployment in Greece was higher than 60% and the economy went into a deflationary spiral, which allowed their economic system to reset.
Is the same about to happen with the AI private credit bubble in the United States? 🇺🇸

item.title: @amitisinvesting: PAUL TUDOR JONES TODAY: - "2027 is going to be a very challenging year for the market." - "Right no...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
PAUL TUDOR JONES TODAY:
- "2027 is going to be a very challenging year for the market."
- "Right now feels exactly like 1999, for me it’s just so clear that we’re on this path that could be great short term but may not be so great long term. I forget that so many people haven’t lived this."
- “I’ll be short the whole year. There just — there’s little value. You had all this issuance, all these IPOs in ’98 and ’99, and really 2000, 2001, 2002. Those were the easiest years to be short because you kept having these unlocks that just kept adding supply to the market.”
PTJ was one of the few investors that began actively shorting the Nasdaq Composite Index in 1999. The question becomes...is he right that we are in 1999, or is it more like 1997? Even Jensen has said that this will all eventually become a bubble but he thinks we have many years before we get there.
I think his comments today are creating more pressure on the semis as many people are trying to navigate 2027 positioning and if the core names in the AI trade are the ones to continue betting on going into next year.
item.content:encoded:
PAUL TUDOR JONES TODAY:

- "2027 is going to be a very challenging year for the market."

- "Right now feels exactly like 1999, for me it’s just so clear that we’re on this path that could be great short term but may not be so great long term. I forget that so many people haven’t lived this."

- “I’ll be short the whole year. There just — there’s little value. You had all this issuance, all these IPOs in ’98 and ’99, and really 2000, 2001, 2002. Those were the easiest years to be short because you kept having these unlocks that just kept adding supply to the market.”

PTJ was one of the few investors that began actively shorting the Nasdaq Composite Index in 1999. The question becomes...is he right that we are in 1999, or is it more like 1997? Even Jensen has said that this will all eventually become a bubble but he thinks we have many years before we get there.

I think his comments today are creating more pressure on the semis as many people are trying to navigate 2027 positioning and if the core names in the AI trade are the ones to continue betting on going into next year.

item.title: @amitisinvesting: A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY. Here's a full recap: 1. Meta $META unveiled Mus...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY.
Here's a full recap:
1. Meta $META unveiled Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, calling them its most capable AI models to date for personal AI agents and software development. Trained at Meta’s gigawatt-scale Prometheus data center, the models combine Active Memory, which carries relevant context across conversations, with Active Focus, enabling agents to persist through complex tasks, explore alternative approaches, and confirm important actions with users. Meta said the models deliver state-of-the-art performance across agent, memory, and coding benchmarks, while supporting professional workflows involving software engineering, legal, financial, and health tasks. Muse Wonder is available today through the Meta Model API and Muse Code, while Muse Wonder Full is available to Muse Code subscribers and will also roll out to the Muse app, alongside stronger safeguards for privacy, malicious instructions, and misuse.
2. Broadcom $AVGO CEO Hock Tan warned that many investors are approaching AI like “casino gamblers,” arguing that capital is increasingly being deployed without a clear understanding of the industry's long-term economics. Tan said the next major constraint on AI may not be chips or power, but capital, as AI developers must prove they can generate sustainable returns from the enormous investments being made today. He also cautioned that some companies are overspending on AI initiatives and emphasized that long-term winners will be those that can turn AI deployments into profitable businesses rather than simply building larger models.
3. The S&P 500 $SPY traded just 18.3M shares today, marking its lowest full-session trading volume since December 26, 2003.
4. Market breadth continues to weaken even as the S&P 500 remains near record highs. 84% of S&P 500 stocks are now trading at least 10% below their all-time highs, despite the index sitting just 0.2% below its record close. Real Estate has been the weakest sector, with 97% of its stocks down at least 10%, followed by Materials (96%), Utilities (94%), and Consumer Discretionary (92%), while Energy (62%), Healthcare (70%), and Information Technology (72%) have held up relatively better. Overall, 59% of S&P 500 stocks are down at least 20% from their highs, 41% are down more than 30%, and 17% have fallen by 50% or more, highlighting the growing divergence between the index and the average stock.
5. Ondas $ONDS and Palantir $PLTR announced the launch of Regna AI, a new company focused on developing specialized AI models for governments and enterprises that want to retain full control over their models, data, and infrastructure. Initially wholly owned by Ondas, Regna will leverage Palantir’s AI platform and model-training infrastructure, with Ondas serving as its first customer. The company's initial focus is on intelligence, surveillance, and defense, developing AI models designed to run directly on drones, ground vehicles, and other edge hardware, even in environments with limited or intermittent connectivity. The companies said initial customer deployments are expected to begin over the coming months.
6. Since the start of 2024, a basket of 42 AI-related stocks has generated 67% of the S&P 500’s total price return, contributing roughly 22 percentage points of the index’s 33% gain over that period. By comparison, the remaining 458 companies have contributed just 11 percentage points. Those same AI leaders have also driven 58% of the S&P 500’s total earnings growth and 81% of all capital expenditure and R&D growth since the beginning of 2024, leaving the rest of the index responsible for only about 20% of investment growth. Meanwhile, just 29% of S&P 500 stocks have outperformed the index over the past 3 years, approaching the roughly 25% participation rate seen during the Dot-Com Bubble.
7. Google $GOOGL is simplifying the Gemini experience by moving toward a single prompt box with no modes or toggles, according to Google VP Josh Woodward. He said the goal is for users to simply tell Gemini what they want and have it automatically determine how to complete the task, reflecting a broader shift in AI user interfaces across the industry. Woodward also hinted that Google is building a “personal, proactive, powerful” version of Gemini, designed to leverage users’ Google data and work more intelligently across their digital lives. He added that Google has heard user requests to make Gemini work more seamlessly with the information they already store in Google services, saying “watch this space” as new capabilities are expected to launch soon.
8. Microsoft $MSFT CEO Satya Nadella announced the company's largest commitment yet to custom AI silicon, saying the Maia chip family will begin scaling to multi-gigawatt deployments starting next calendar year and become the primary inference platform for Microsoft's products and services. Microsoft also introduced Maia 300, which Nadella said delivers 40% more tokens per watt than leading GPU-based systems. The company is already deploying Maia 200 across the U.S., Europe, and Australia, achieving up to 1.7x more tokens per watt for workloads powering Teams and Copilot. Nadella said Microsoft's strategy is to continue improving full-stack efficiency while also incorporating the latest innovations from across the broader AI ecosystem.
9. Global physical gold-backed ETFs attracted a record $30.7B of inflows during Q3 2026, marking the largest quarterly inflow on record. September alone saw $10B of inflows, following $17.9B in August, the second-largest monthly inflow ever recorded. As a result, global gold ETF holdings increased by 67 tonnes in September to a record 4,256 tonnes, surpassing the previous high of 4,176 tonnes set in February. Year-to-date, gold ETFs have attracted $38.5B in inflows—equivalent to 226 tonnes of additional gold holdings—with demand positive across every region. UK-listed funds have led country-level inflows with $9.5B, overtaking China, highlighting exceptionally strong global demand for gold.
10. Anthropic said it has reduced the amount of data harvested through AI distillation attacks by approximately 90–99% after deploying new anti-distillation defenses. The company said Zhipu attempted to distill capabilities from Claude Fable 5, but switched to an older Claude model after encountering stronger cyber safeguards. Anthropic also revealed it has turned away meaningful revenue and trillions of tokens' worth of paying traffic from suspected distillers, prioritizing model security over short-term revenue. The company said preventing unauthorized model distillation is a key national security issue, as frontier AI capabilities can otherwise be replicated at a fraction of the cost and integrated into foreign AI systems.
11. The top 10 most active options today by contracts traded were $NVDA with 2.8M contracts, $TSLA with 1.5M contracts, $META with 1.3M contracts, $MU with 1.2M contracts, $AAPL with 1.1M contracts, $SPCX with 998K contracts, $INTC with 778K contracts, $AMZN with 680K contracts, $MSFT with 648K contracts, and $AMD with 598K contracts.
12. BlackRock has downgraded U.S. equities to Neutral while turning more constructive on U.S. Treasuries, according to a new outlook from the BlackRock Investment Institute and CIO Rick Rieder. The firm upgraded short-term Treasuries to Overweight, raised long-term Treasuries to Neutral from Underweight, and cut U.S. stocks to Neutral after maintaining an Overweight stance for an extended period. BlackRock emphasized that the move reflects near-term risk management, not a change in its long-term outlook, stating it remains bullish on AI and that its core investment convictions are unchanged.
WALL STREET IS THE GREATEST SHOW ON EARTH.

item.title: @FinanceLancelot: Bank of America CCC & Lower High Yield is surging exactly like February 2020, August 2015 and 2008....
item.dc:creator: @FinanceLancelot
item.description:
Bank of America CCC & Lower High Yield is surging exactly like February 2020, August 2015 and 2008.
All of these were major market events.
BAMLH0A3HYC measures the extra yield investors are demanding to hold distressed, below-investment-grade corporate debt (rated CCC or lower) compared to the risk-free Treasury yield.
This gives us a great idea what's happening behind the scenes in the private credit market.
Basically, defaults are surging and availability of credit is shrinking in reaction, which causes a feedback loop of rising defaults reducing credit causing further rising defaults.
On top of this, you're getting high fuel prices causing demand destruction in consumer discretionary spending.

item.title: @amitisinvesting: $MU $SNDK Are the CXMT memory optimization headlines a real threat to the memory trade or is it jus...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
$MU $SNDK
Are the CXMT memory optimization headlines a real threat to the memory trade or is it just another architecture that will lead to more usage of tokens which will make up for pricing power in volumes?
The memory trade, like the semis in general, has been fragile enough for these headlines to affect them almost every week.
We saw this last week with the HDD manufacturing capacity increase by Toshiba that took $STX and $WDC down 20%.
At some point, the street either is going to believe these names are undervalued relative to their growth or they are going to give up on trying to be optimistic when a new headline around memory efficiency comes out every other week and reminds them about how traditionally cyclical the business is.

item.title: @amitisinvesting: $ONDS I agree with much of what Steve is saying here below. Have been looking deeper into Ondas as...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
$ONDS
I agree with much of what Steve is saying here below. Have been looking deeper into Ondas as well.
The biggest issue is dilution, which obviously has kept the stock down. It’s been the biggest bear case.
However, the combination of a $1.5T defense budget + the broader defense conglomerate that Ondas is creating (funded via dilution) + 52-week lows + rapid growth with GAAP net income on the horizon makes this interesting.
The biggest thing getting my attention with Ondas is the $PLTR Palantir partnership and I am diving deeper into why/how both companies are working together in order to scale the broader OS that is coming together as a result of the combination.
Open to hearing more perspectives on this name, I know there is a passionate retail base that is likely very annoyed because of dilution but I am trying to envision what it takes for Ondas to be a $25B company one day and how much growth could be achieved synergistically with their acquisitions to make it happen.
item.content:encoded:
$ONDS

I agree with much of what Steve is saying here below. Have been looking deeper into Ondas as well.

The biggest issue is dilution, which obviously has kept the stock down. It’s been the biggest bear case.

However, the combination of a $1.5T defense budget + the broader defense conglomerate that Ondas is creating (funded via dilution) + 52-week lows + rapid growth with GAAP net income on the horizon makes this interesting.

The biggest thing getting my attention with Ondas is the $PLTR Palantir partnership and I am diving deeper into why/how both companies are working together in order to scale the broader OS that is coming together as a result of the combination.

Open to hearing more perspectives on this name, I know there is a passionate retail base that is likely very annoyed because of dilution but I am trying to envision what it takes for Ondas to be a $25B company one day and how much growth could be achieved synergistically with their acquisitions to make it happen.

item.title: @FinanceLancelot: Getting technical: All indicators are saying the rally began on Friday, similar to April 2026. Nasd...
item.dc:creator: @FinanceLancelot
item.description:
Getting technical: All indicators are saying the rally began on Friday, similar to April 2026.
Nasdaq New Highs - New Lows has bottomed and is currently in uptrend.
S&P 500 Volume McClellan Summation Index is another indicator suggesting markets will rally into the midterms.
Finally, the most reliable indicator S&P 500 50 day / 200 day also is clearly pumping upward.
Remember what I said before though, VIXEQ is moving upward but COR1M is stagnant. VIXEQ measures individual stock volatility while COR1M measures correlation in the index.
In plain English, when VIXEQ is rising while COR1M is flat means a handful of stocks are driving the index upward while most of the stocks can be flat or falling.
This is a stock pickers market, with low correlation and violent moves in individual stocks.

item.title: @FinanceLancelot: The U.S. 10 year treasuries had a very strong auction this week among the private sector. How can w...
item.dc:creator: @FinanceLancelot
item.description:
The U.S. 10 year treasuries had a very strong auction this week among the private sector.
How can we tell this? Primary dealers are obligated to buy U.S. treasuries when the market doesn't.
This week we saw primary dealer Z-score fall to -2.07, which implies the private sector finds the 10 year yield attractive at this level.
This could also imply there's a need for collateral in the banking system.
This is bullish for market liquidity for multiple reasons because if yields have stopped rising, lending risk falls.
A long as we don't see treasury yields suddenly start to fall, that would imply "risk off" in the markets.

Here's a full recap:
1. OpenAI told investors its annualized revenue was approaching $50B at the end of September, according to the Financial Times, below the roughly $70B figure that had been widely reported last month. The discrepancy reportedly reflects differences in accounting methods, with Anthropic including revenue generated through cloud partners such as AWS and Google Cloud, while OpenAI does not. Investors had attempted to adjust OpenAI’s figures to make them comparable with Anthropic’s, contributing to the higher estimate. The report weighed on AI infrastructure sentiment, with several semiconductor stocks falling roughly 5–7% as investors reassessed near-term AI spending expectations. OpenAI declined to comment.
2. The September FOMC meeting minutes showed that most Federal Reserve officials expect another interest rate hike by year-end, reinforcing the central bank’s higher-for-longer stance. All 19 Fed officials supported the September rate hike, reflecting unanimous concern that inflation remains above target. The minutes also said almost all policymakers believe inflation risks remain tilted to the upside, with several officials warning that the accelerating AI investment boom could increase demand faster than supply, adding to inflationary pressures.
3. Elon Musk said today that he sees an extraordinary long-term future for $SPCX SpaceX, writing: “This will sound super crazy, but I see a path to SpaceX being worth orders of magnitude more than the current Earth economy.”
4. Goldman Sachs upgraded Palantir $PLTR to Buy with a $230 price target, while Barclays initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a $265 price target. Goldman argued that Palantir’s total addressable market is entering another step-function expansion, driven by the rise of sovereign AI, bespoke enterprise AI applications, and the company’s increasing verticalization strategy. The firm also highlighted Palantir’s Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) model as a key competitive advantage, noting that its tight feedback loop between customer deployments and product development has become so refined that Palantir is now able to automate portions of the FDE workflow with AI-powered FDEs. Goldman believes these dynamics further strengthen Palantir’s long-term competitive position as enterprise AI adoption accelerates.
5. Zeta $ZETA unveiled AthenaOS, an enterprise intelligence operating system designed to dynamically organize AI, applications, and workflows around a specific business objective by combining proprietary enterprise knowledge with intelligence from the Zeta Data Cloud. The company also introduced Athena MCP, which allows Athena’s intelligence to plug directly into existing enterprise tools, including ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini, while preserving enterprise data governance and control. Zeta also launched the Athena Inference Model (AIM), a suite of specialized AI models built with Fireworks using NVIDIA Nemotron, and said it has begun developing a specialized AI chip and supporting data center infrastructure with a leading semiconductor partner through a capital-light approach. AthenaOS is currently in limited internal beta, with a public beta planned later this year and general availability targeted for Q1 2027.
6. Starbucks $SBUX has reportedly explored a potential takeover of Chipotle $CMG in what would rank among the largest restaurant acquisitions ever. A combination could significantly accelerate Chipotle’s international expansion by leveraging Starbucks’ global network of more than 41,000 stores, established licensing partners, and extensive real estate relationships. At the same time, any transaction would face substantial financing, integration, and execution challenges given the size of the deal and the complexity of combining two of the world's largest restaurant brands.
7. The top 10 most active options today by contracts traded were $NVDA with 2.9M contracts, $TSLA with 1.3M contracts, $INTC with 1.2M contracts, $MU with 1.1M contracts, $AAPL with 1.0M contracts, $SPCX with 1.0M contracts, $PLTR with 927K contracts, $AMZN with 635K contracts, $ORCL with 635K contracts, and $IREN with 612K contracts.
8. The U.S. Pentagon has reportedly instructed the military to complete preparations for a potential resumption of major combat operations against Iran, according to Axios. U.S. and Israeli sources told the outlet that renewed operations could occur before the midterm elections, while a White House official said President Trump “has all options available at any time.” The report also said Trump's national security team met at Camp David on Friday to discuss possible scenarios for restarting large-scale military operations. The developments come as the administration continues weighing both military and diplomatic options in its approach toward Iran.
9. Broadcom $AVGO is reportedly seeking more than $50B in financing for OpenAI’s custom AI chip program, according to the Wall Street Journal, with Apollo and Blackstone among the firms approached to participate. The financing could support several gigawatts of custom AI chip capacity, with a transaction targeted before year-end, though discussions remain preliminary and the size could change. OpenAI’s internally developed chip initiative, known as “Nexus,” includes its first two generations, “Jalapeño” and “Serrano,” and builds on the companies’ previously announced plan to deploy 10 GW of custom AI chips using Broadcom’s networking technology between the second half of 2026 and 2029.
10. Bitcoin $BTC fell to around $81,000 down roughly 3% on the day and about 6–8% from the $87,000 highs reached earlier this week, with an intraday low near $80,300. The selloff appears to be a broad risk-off move rather than the result of a single headline, driven by Brent crude above $105, rising inflation concerns, expectations for another Fed rate hike after the September FOMC minutes and comments from Governor Christopher Waller, and a 10-year Treasury yield near 5.3%. Pressure was compounded by roughly $485M in U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF outflows on October 7, approximately $1–1.16B in crypto liquidations, mostly long positions, and blockchain data showing wallets linked to the U.S. government moving about 12,267 BTC from a seized Bitfinex wallet, adding to concerns about potential future supply. Altcoins underperformed Bitcoin throughout the session, consistent with a broader leverage-driven unwind across the crypto market.
11. Since the start of 2025, U.S. nonfarm payrolls have been revised lower in 16 of the last 20 months, removing a cumulative 793,000 jobs from previously reported figures, an average downward revision of roughly 39,650 jobs per month. The latest revisions reduced July and August payrolls by a combined 60,000 jobs, continuing a pattern of consistent downward revisions that has persisted since 2023. If that average revision were applied to the initially reported 29,000 jobs added in September, it would imply a decline of roughly 10,650 jobs instead. That would mark the third monthly contraction in payrolls during 2026, following declines of 156,000 in February and 10,000 in July.
12. SpaceX $SPCX has agreed to acquire Grain Management’s nationwide portfolio of 800 MHz low-band spectrum licenses, a move Elon Musk called “the last critical piece of the spectrum puzzle” needed for Starlink to become a major U.S. mobile carrier. The company plans to combine its satellite network with a terrestrial mobile network, using the newly acquired low-band spectrum alongside Starlink’s existing 2 GHz holdings to improve indoor coverage and expand service into areas with weak or no cellular reception. Separately, the FCC approved a new constellation of 15,000 SpaceX satellites for direct-to-device mobile services, further advancing Starlink’s wireless ambitions. The announcement pressured telecom stocks after hours, with AT&T $T falling 6.75%, Verizon $VZ down 5%, and T-Mobile $TMUS declining 5.4%, as investors weighed the prospect of a new nationwide competitor. The spectrum acquisition remains subject to FCC approval and other customary closing conditions, with financial terms undisclosed.
WALL STREET IS THE GREATEST SHOW ON EARTH.

item.title: @FinanceLancelot: The FOMC minutes were split about the reasons why they hiked in September: 1) Some argued a higher...
item.dc:creator: @FinanceLancelot
item.description:
The FOMC minutes were split about the reasons why they hiked in September:
1) Some argued a higher rate would reduce the chance that inflation above 2% would become unanchored
2) A couple focused on stopping sector-specific price increases
Here's the most interesting part. They basically outlined that 1 more rate hike is in the cards before year end.
The next meetings are October 28 and December 9.
By doing 1 rate raise Kevin Warsh has demonstrated he's a hawk.
They're unlikely to raise rates right before the election, which means there won't be any surprises before December.
By that point, if the market corrects or flash crashes then the Federal Reserve will be cutting instead of raising.

item.title: @amitisinvesting: A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY. Here's a full recap: 1. SpaceX $SPCX is reporte...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY.
Here's a full recap:
1. SpaceX $SPCX is reportedly seeking $40B in financing, led by Apollo, to fund a massive purchase of NVIDIA $NVDA AI chips, according to the Financial Times. The proposed financing includes roughly $10B in bank loans and $30B of investment-grade debt, with the transaction expected to close in 2027. Elon Musk said in August that SpaceX had “decided to build exclusively on NVIDIA,” specifically highlighting the company's Vera Rubin architecture as SpaceX accelerates investment in AI compute and data center infrastructure.
2. AMD $AMD CEO Lisa Su said AI compute demand continues to outpace supply and expects strong demand to persist for the next several years, with AMD planning to substantially increase supply in 2027. Su said AMD has already expanded supply this year but “could definitely use more,” thanking TSMC for bringing additional manufacturing capacity online while noting that memory remains broadly supply constrained. She added that AMD is working closely with memory suppliers and customers to ensure capacity ramps in sync while keeping its current business model unchanged. Su also described Taiwan as “very critical” to AMD, saying the company plans to increase its investment there while continuing to explore new packaging technologies.
3. Uber $UBER is acquiring ezCater for $2.3B in cash, expanding Uber Eats into the workplace catering market. ezCater has more than 140,000 restaurant partners, generates over $2.5B in trailing 12-month gross bookings, is growing at a high-teens annual rate, and has average order values above $400 while remaining profitable on a non-GAAP operating income basis. Following the acquisition, ezCater will be integrated with Uber Eats and Uber for Business, strengthening Uber's position in high-value group orders and enterprise food delivery. Uber said the transaction is expected to be margin accretive.
4. Penguin Solutions $PENG just delivered a blowout Q4, with revenue of $566.7M versus $521M expected, up 68% YoY, while adjusted EPS of $1.00 beat the $0.77 estimate by roughly 30%. Adjusted EBITDA surged 115% YoY to $93M, while FY2026 revenue reached $1.73B and adjusted EPS came in at $2.87, both ahead of expectations. The bigger story was guidance, with Penguin now expecting FY2027 revenue around a $2.43B midpoint, implying roughly 40% growth and coming in about 10% above consensus, while adjusted EPS is expected at $4.45 ± $0.70 versus $3.38 expected. AI infrastructure momentum also accelerated sharply, with 6 new data center customers added in Q4, including 4 neoclouds, alongside a customer deployment involving a 36,000-GPU AI factory in Norway and another platform built around NVIDIA GB300 NVL72. Management said performance accelerated significantly in the second half following the launch of its AI Factory Platform and increased focus on the data center market.
5. Google $GOOGL and Constellation Energy $CEG signed a 20-year agreement to add 890 MW of nuclear power to the PJM grid through upgrades at 11 reactors, backed by $4.3B of investment. The companies also signed a separate 15-year power supply agreement covering an additional 2.7 GW, with the first reactor uprate expected to come online in 2028. The announcement lifted sentiment across the power sector, with Vistra $VST surging 12% as investors continued to price in growing electricity demand from AI data centers and hyperscale infrastructure.
6. The top 10 most active options today by contracts traded were $NVDA with 2.4M contracts, $TSLA with 1.2M contracts, $SPCX with 1.1M contracts, $INTC with 914K contracts, $AAPL with 802K contracts, $AMZN with 798K contracts, $AVGO with 702K contracts, $MU with 699K contracts, $AMD with 627K contracts, and $MSFT with 511K contracts.
7. Marvell $MRVL raised its long-term outlook, now expecting approximately $20B in FY2028 revenue, up from its prior $18B target, and projecting $70B–$90B in annual revenue by FY2031. CEO Matt Murphy also significantly increased the company's estimate for the AI market opportunity, now forecasting a roughly $400B AI market by 2030, more than 4x its previous $94B opportunity estimate for 2028. The updated outlook reflects Marvell's growing confidence in sustained AI infrastructure spending and demand for custom silicon, networking, and data center connectivity solutions.
8. CrowdStrike $CRWD is expanding its cybersecurity startup accelerator with AWS and NVIDIA, with the 2027 program focused on startups building security solutions for the agentic AI era. Participants will receive access to CrowdStrike Falcon Foundry and APIs, AWS technical and go-to-market support, and NVIDIA Inception resources. The accelerator has supported more than 90 startups to date, which have collectively raised nearly $1B. Up to 10 finalists will present at RSAC 2027, with participating companies also eligible for potential investment from CrowdStrike’s Falcon Fund.
9. Apple $AAPL is reportedly making a major push into the smart home, developing a new doorbell, smart lock, thermostat, and other accessories in partnership with LG Electronics. The products are expected to work alongside Apple’s upcoming smart home hub, updated HomePod mini, and refreshed Apple TV, giving the company a much broader ecosystem for home control, security, and automation. The home hub, new HomePod mini, and updated Apple TV are expected to be unveiled on October 13. The move would push Apple beyond HomeKit software and third-party accessories and toward a more vertically integrated smart-home platform built around its own hardware, software, services, and ecosystem.
10. Nokia $NOK CEO Justin Hotard said AI infrastructure demand continues to outpace supply, arguing that supply constraints—not weak demand—are the primary factor limiting deployment. “I don’t think you can say in any manner we’re overbuilding today,” Hotard said, adding that if Nokia and its customers could build 2x faster, they likely would. He said that gives him confidence the industry is “still in the early days” of the AI infrastructure buildout and argued demand does not depend on a constant stream of new frontier AI models. According to Hotard, even without another major frontier model release over the next three years, the industry could still make tremendous progress deploying today's AI technology, with memory supply and power availability remaining the biggest constraints.
11. Ray Dalio is warning that the U.S. could be headed toward a debt crisis within the next 2–3 years, arguing that persistent deficits, rising interest costs, and a shrinking pool of available savings are pushing the country toward the limits of its debt cycle. He said the issue is not any specific Treasury yield, but rather the growing mismatch between the amount of capital the government needs to borrow and the willingness of investors, particularly foreign creditors, to finance it. Dalio said he is currently short government debt and long gold, recommending that diversified portfolios hold 5–15% in gold, while noting he owns only about 1% in Bitcoin and remains skeptical of digital assets. On AI, Dalio said investors will either “ride the crest of the AI wave or drown under it,” arguing that AI can increasingly handle the entire investment process, but that humans still need to define the decision framework and challenge the model’s conclusions rather than blindly accepting them.
12. Cantor Fitzgerald said the recent selloff in Western Digital $WDC and Seagate $STX following Toshiba’s plan to double nearline hard drive capacity by FY2027 is overdone and presents a buying opportunity. The firm argues Toshiba’s expansion is unlikely to materially change industry supply because demand from AI and data centers continues to outpace capacity, Toshiba’s technology still trails competitors, and long-term agreements support pricing stability for WDC and STX. The selloff in those names could have also been the reason for the broader memory weakness in the sector affecting companies like $MU Micron, $SNDK Sandisk, and $SKHY SK Hynix. Cantor also questioned Toshiba’s ability to execute its expansion plans, noting a similar effort announced in 2022 failed to materialize. The firm expects AI-driven data generation to keep nearline HDD demand ahead of supply through 2030 and beyond, supporting 70%+ long-term margins, expanding free cash flow, and continued share repurchases for both WDC and STX, which remain its Top Picks.
WALL STREET IS THE GREATEST SHOW ON EARTH.

item.title: @amitisinvesting: DALIO: WE ARE 36 MONTHS AWAY FROM A US DEBT CRISIS I feel like he's been legitimately saying this f...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
DALIO: WE ARE 36 MONTHS AWAY FROM A US DEBT CRISIS
I feel like he's been legitimately saying this for years at this point, now to his credit, yields are the highest they have been in 20 years so the probability of debt crisis *feels* more likely given bonds are losing their value globally.
However, I also think that AI is going to be the biggest DEFLATIONARY force we have ever seen in human history over the next decade which should bring inflation down, the cost of capital down, GDP up, and gives the global economy a way to work through our debt.
Just feels like this technology revolution could be the solution to some of our problems even if in the short term, it creates many headwinds for global debt based on the rising cost of capital with corporate bonds competing with treasuries.

item.title: @amitisinvesting: GOOD MORNING. Bond Yields are down. Oil hit a 2-week low. Nvidia is at an all time high. The S&P ju...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
GOOD MORNING.
Bond Yields are down. Oil hit a 2-week low. Nvidia is at an all time high. The S&P just passed an time high in the pre-markets after adding $500B of marketcap yesterday and now being worth over $70T of marketcap in total.
This is all happening in the midst of some of the worst breadth underneath the index with most sectors like financials and consumer discretionary not really participating. Even many semiconductor names, like the memory stocks, are not fully participating or back to their ATHs.
Tech is the story, particularly large cap tech like $TSM $NVDA $META $GOOGL $SPCX $AMD $AVGO $MSFT, and we are seeing those names bring the index to record highs.
If we are seeing these levels on the index with Oil still up massively on the year and Yields still at the highest in 3 years, the question becomes if the market has this wrong and this is a bull trap or if the market is front-running the inevitable decline in yields and oil, which would also imply the chances for a Fed hike will come down substantially.
If it is the latter, things can get really, really fun.
item.content:encoded:
GOOD MORNING.

Bond Yields are down. Oil hit a 2-week low. Nvidia is at an all time high. The S&P just passed an time high in the pre-markets after adding $500B of marketcap yesterday and now being worth over $70T of marketcap in total.

This is all happening in the midst of some of the worst breadth underneath the index with most sectors like financials and consumer discretionary not really participating. Even many semiconductor names, like the memory stocks, are not fully participating or back to their ATHs.

Tech is the story, particularly large cap tech like $TSM $NVDA $META $GOOGL $SPCX $AMD $AVGO $MSFT, and we are seeing those names bring the index to record highs.

If we are seeing these levels on the index with Oil still up massively on the year and Yields still at the highest in 3 years, the question becomes if the market has this wrong and this is a bull trap or if the market is front-running the inevitable decline in yields and oil, which would also imply the chances for a Fed hike will come down substantially.

If it is the latter, things can get really, really fun.

item.title: @I_Am_The_ICT: When markets are at all time highs, it can be hard to trust buying. So how do I do it? Same rules,...
item.dc:creator: @I_Am_The_ICT
item.description:
When markets are at all time highs, it can be hard to trust buying. So how do I do it?
Same rules, wait for sellside liquidity to be purged, enter a shorter intraday Discount... key level at key timing.
I never rush to chase it. I never regret a missed run. I never force my will on Price at ATHs.
Patience must be the driving force, more than ever.
For some, the wisest decision is stillness... emphasis on "some".
