item.title: @amitisinvesting: A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY. Here's a full recap: 1. SpaceX $SPCX rose about...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY.
Here's a full recap:
1. SpaceX $SPCX rose about 7.6% on Monday to roughly $171.09 after Elon Musk confirmed that discussions with TSMC are real, though still in the early stages. The talks follow reports that TSMC is exploring a role in Terafab, the Texas chip venture tied to Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI, which could eventually invest $119B to manufacture chips for products including Optimus, Cybercab, and future AI infrastructure. The prospect of TSMC participating was viewed as strengthening SpaceX’s long-term AI chip supply strategy and potentially reducing Intel’s future role in the project, helping send Intel shares lower while TSMC reached a new all-time high. A reiterated Morgan Stanley Overweight rating and $300 price target provided additional support for the stock.
2. Meta $META and Microsoft $MSFT are reportedly reducing internal use of Anthropic’s Claude as they increasingly shift employees toward their own AI tools, according to The Information. Microsoft had been on pace to spend at least $1B annually on internal Claude usage earlier this year but has since reduced that level by more than one-third. At Meta, the number of Claude Code users has reportedly fallen to about 30,000 from roughly 60,000 earlier this year, while MetaCode now has more than 30,000 users and Muse Code has surpassed 6,000. Despite the shift, Meta still spent more than $105M on Claude Code over a recent 28-day period.
3. JPMorgan expects the memory market $MU $SNDK $WDC $SKHY $STX to remain supply-constrained through at least 2028, with customer order discussions already extending as far out as 2031. The firm forecasts HBM bit demand to grow 63%, non-HBM server DRAM demand to increase 37%, and CY2027 HBM blended ASPs to rise 54% year over year. JPM also believes Micron’s expectation of having more than 35% of revenue covered by long-term supply agreements through 2030 may prove conservative, noting that several Asian memory manufacturers already have 50%+ of their capacity secured under similar long-term agreements.
4. RBC Capital Markets reiterated its Outperform rating on Zeta $ZETA and raised its price target to $40 from $31, implying roughly 22.6% upside. Analyst Matt Swanson said recent investor meetings highlighted growing momentum around strategic partnerships and adoption of Athena, while emphasizing that RBC does not believe these opportunities are materially reflected in either current guidance or the company’s 2030 outlook. RBC also argued that Zeta has increasingly differentiated itself from traditional ad-tech peers and is now being valued more like a software company. The latest increase marks RBC’s third price target raise on Zeta this calendar year.
5. Ondas $ONDS secured a $56M order for Electronic Safe & Arm Devices (ESADs) supporting a European loitering munition program. The contract will be fulfilled through Ondas' recently acquired Bron Technologies and GATE Technologies businesses. ESADs manage a munition’s safety, arming, and initiation functions, with production set to move forward using technology that has already been qualified for deployment. The award further expands Ondas’ presence in the growing European defense and precision munitions market.
6. Bank of America, Citi, and Morgan Stanley have begun syndicating a $60B debt package tied to Anthropic’s lease of Google-designed TPUs supplied through Broadcom $AVGO, making it the largest chip-financing deal to date. The package includes $42B of senior secured debt backed by Broadcom and $18B of junior debt without Broadcom guarantees, with Blackstone already committing roughly $9B to the junior tranche. The financing is expected to fund Anthropic’s 2027 chip orders, with Broadcom’s support helping reduce borrowing costs and potentially allowing the senior debt to be refinanced into the investment-grade market. The deal centers on Google $GOOGL TPUs, developed with Broadcom as an alternative to NVIDIA $NVDA GPUs for large-scale AI workloads, while Broadcom filings also indicate Anthropic could issue up to $42B of convertible notes to Broadcom to cover future lease payments.
7. U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) inventories fell another 767,000 barrels last week to 283M barrels, the lowest level since 1982. The decline marks the 28th consecutive weekly drawdown, leaving the SPR down nearly 133M barrels from its recent peak. As a result, America's emergency crude oil reserves continue to sit near their lowest levels in more than four decades, underscoring the limited strategic buffer available despite elevated geopolitical risks.
8. The Consumer Confidence Index fell 6.7 points in September to 81.9, its lowest level since April 2014, marking a fourth consecutive monthly decline and an 11.2-point drop over that period. The Present Situation Index declined 7.9 points to 109.3, its weakest reading since February 2021, while the Expectations Index fell 5.9 points to 63.6, its lowest since April 2025 and a third straight monthly decline. Confidence has weakened across all age groups and nearly all income brackets over the past six months. Consumers increasingly cited high prices, the cost of goods and services, and oil and gasoline prices as the primary factors weighing on the economic outlook.
9. Brazilian markets rallied after Flávio Bolsonaro finished ahead of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the first round of Brazil’s presidential election, with investors reacting positively to the prospect of a more market-friendly policy agenda ahead of the October 25 runoff. Brazilian assets including Nu Holdings $NU, the iShares MSCI Brazil ETF $EWZ, and other Brazil-exposed equities such as MercadoLibre $MELI outperformed following the result. The market reaction reflected optimism around potential fiscal and economic policy changes, though the election remains undecided with a runoff still to come.
10. The top 10 most active options today by contracts traded were $NVDA with 4.0M contracts, $TSLA with 3.2M contracts, $SPCX with 1.7M contracts, $AAPL with 1.1M contracts, $MSFT with 874K contracts, $MU with 872K contracts, $AMZN with 844K contracts, $INTC with 835K contracts, $META with 790K contracts, and $GOOGL with 502K contracts.
11. OpenAI is reportedly in talks with UAE investment funds, including MGX, and BlackRock $BLK to anchor a new $30B+ funding round at a valuation of roughly $1.4T, according to Bloomberg. UAE investors have discussed contributing as much as $10B collectively, while existing backers Thrive Capital and Andreessen Horowitz are also considering additional investments, alongside discussions with the University of California endowment. Rather than negotiating with a lead investor, OpenAI is reportedly presenting investors with a fixed ~$1.4T pre-money valuation. The fundraising comes as OpenAI continues to delay an IPO until at least 2027 while raising unprecedented amounts of capital to fund AI model development and large-scale infrastructure expansion.
12. Melius upgraded Microsoft $MSFT to Buy with a $665 price target, arguing that growing concerns around AI safety are actually strengthening Microsoft's competitive position. The firm said enterprises are increasingly choosing to spend on a secure AI wrapper that can route models to the right tasks, manage AI agents, and provide governance rather than relying directly on frontier AI labs. Melius believes Satya Nadella and Microsoft's leadership are becoming the "adults in charge" for AI security and governance, and now expects Azure revenue growth to accelerate to above 50% by F4Q27.
WALL STREET IS THE GREATEST SHOW ON EARTH.

Microsoft had been on pace to spend at least $1B annually on internal Claude usage earlier this year but has since reduced that level by more than one-third. At Meta, the number of Claude Code users has reportedly fallen to about 30,000 from roughly 60,000 earlier this year, while MetaCode now has more than 30,000 users and Muse Code has surpassed 6,000. Despite the shift, Meta still spent more than $105M on Claude Code over a recent 28-day period.

3. JPMorgan expects the memory market $MU $SNDK $WDC $SKHY $STX to remain supply-constrained through at least 2028, with customer order discussions already extending as far out as 2031. The firm forecasts HBM bit demand to grow 63%, non-HBM server DRAM demand to increase 37%, and CY2027 HBM blended ASPs to rise 54% year over year. JPM also believes Micron’s expectation of having more than 35% of revenue covered by long-term supply agreements through 2030 may prove conservative, noting that several Asian memory manufacturers already have 50%+ of their capacity secured under similar long-term agreements.

4. RBC Capital Markets reiterated its Outperform rating on Zeta $ZETA and raised its price target to $40 from $31, implying roughly 22.6% upside. Analyst Matt Swanson said recent investor meetings highlighted growing momentum around strategic partnerships and adoption of Athena, while emphasizing that RBC does not believe these opportunities are materially reflected in either current guidance or the company’s 2030 outlook. RBC also argued that Zeta has increasingly differentiated itself from traditional ad-tech peers and is now being valued more like a software company. The latest increase marks RBC’s third price target raise on Zeta this calendar year.

5. Ondas $ONDS secured a $56M order for Electronic Safe & Arm Devices (ESADs) supporting a European loitering munition program. The contract will be fulfilled through Ondas' recently acquired Bron Technologies and GATE Technologies businesses. ESADs manage a munition’s safety, arming, and initiation functions, with production set to move forward using technology that has already been qualified for deployment. The award further expands Ondas’ presence in the growing European defense and precision munitions market.

6. Bank of America, Citi, and Morgan Stanley have begun syndicating a $60B debt package tied to Anthropic’s lease of Google-designed TPUs supplied through Broadcom $AVGO, making it the largest chip-financing deal to date. The package includes $42B of senior secured debt backed by Broadcom and $18B of junior debt without Broadcom guarantees, with Blackstone already committing roughly $9B to the junior tranche. The financing is expected to fund Anthropic’s 2027 chip orders, with Broadcom’s support helping reduce borrowing costs and potentially allowing the senior debt to be refinanced into the investment-grade market. The deal centers on Google $GOOGL TPUs, developed with Broadcom as an alternative to NVIDIA $NVDA GPUs for large-scale AI workloads, while Broadcom filings also indicate Anthropic could issue up to $42B of convertible notes to Broadcom to cover future lease payments.

7. U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) inventories fell another 767,000 barrels last week to 283M barrels, the lowest level since 1982. The decline marks the 28th consecutive weekly drawdown, leaving the SPR down nearly 133M barrels from its recent peak. As a result, America's emergency crude oil reserves continue to sit near their lowest levels in more than four decades, underscoring the limited strategic buffer available despite elevated geopolitical risks.

8. The Consumer Confidence Index fell 6.7 points in September to 81.9, its lowest level since April 2014, marking a fourth consecutive monthly decline and an 11.2-point drop over that period. The Present Situation Index declined 7.9 points to 109.3, its weakest reading since February 2021, while the Expectations Index fell 5.9 points to 63.6, its lowest since April 2025 and a third straight monthly decline. Confidence has weakened across all age groups and nearly all income brackets over the past six months. Consumers increasingly cited high prices, the cost of goods and services, and oil and gasoline prices as the primary factors weighing on the economic outlook.

9. Brazilian markets rallied after Flávio Bolsonaro finished ahead of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the first round of Brazil’s presidential election, with investors reacting positively to the prospect of a more market-friendly policy agenda ahead of the October 25 runoff. Brazilian assets including Nu Holdings $NU, the iShares MSCI Brazil ETF $EWZ, and other Brazil-exposed equities such as MercadoLibre $MELI outperformed following the result. The market reaction reflected optimism around potential fiscal and economic policy changes, though the election remains undecided with a runoff still to come.

10. The top 10 most active options today by contracts traded were $NVDA with 4.0M contracts, $TSLA with 3.2M contracts, $SPCX with 1.7M contracts, $AAPL with 1.1M contracts, $MSFT with 874K contracts, $MU with 872K contracts, $AMZN with 844K contracts, $INTC with 835K contracts, $META with 790K contracts, and $GOOGL with 502K contracts.

11. OpenAI is reportedly in talks with UAE investment funds, including MGX, and BlackRock $BLK to anchor a new $30B+ funding round at a valuation of roughly $1.4T, according to Bloomberg. UAE investors have discussed contributing as much as $10B collectively, while existing backers Thrive Capital and Andreessen Horowitz are also considering additional investments, alongside discussions with the University of California endowment. Rather than negotiating with a lead investor, OpenAI is reportedly presenting investors with a fixed ~$1.4T pre-money valuation. The fundraising comes as OpenAI continues to delay an IPO until at least 2027 while raising unprecedented amounts of capital to fund AI model development and large-scale infrastructure expansion.

12. Melius upgraded Microsoft $MSFT to Buy with a $665 price target, arguing that growing concerns around AI safety are actually strengthening Microsoft's competitive position. The firm said enterprises are increasingly choosing to spend on a secure AI wrapper that can route models to the right tasks, manage AI agents, and provide governance rather than relying directly on frontier AI labs. Melius believes Satya Nadella and Microsoft's leadership are becoming the "adults in charge" for AI security and governance, and now expects Azure revenue growth to accelerate to above 50% by F4Q27.

WALL STREET IS THE GREATEST SHOW ON EARTH.

item.title: @FinanceLancelot: All the technical indicators are suggesting the S&P 500, Russell 2000 and Dow Jones stocks above th...
item.dc:creator: @FinanceLancelot
item.description:
All the technical indicators are suggesting the S&P 500, Russell 2000 and Dow Jones stocks above the 50 day moving average are ready for a rebound.
Fascinating though, the Nasdaq looks particularly weak.
What's interesting here is the PMO indicator is still deteriorating, which means market breadth is still getting worse.
This means this next rally will be a stock pickers rally, instead of broad upward move. It will be highly concentrated in a few market leaders that will drag the index up, while the rest languish on the sidelines.
This is classic topping behavior. High concentration + vertical moves in a handful of stock.
We'll know in a few weeks if I'm correct.

This is classic topping behavior. High concentration + vertical moves in a handful of stock.

We'll know in a few weeks if I'm correct.

BREAKING: The White House says they are monitoring a plague outbreak in Russia
Unlike bubonic plague, pneumonic plague accounts for less that 2% of cases is spread from person to person through the respiratory track.
The survival rate is 17% or lower with prompt antibiotic treatment given within 24 hours of first symptoms.
The last major pneumonic plague outbreak was Madagascar in August 2017.
5 hospitals have been closed for quarantines in Siberia.
A 28-year-old lab technician, died yesterday after breaking a test tube with live Yersinia pestis the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute while handling samples.
Mask mandates have now been introduced at businesses in Irkutsk. https://x.com/FinanceLancelot/status/1523499725042946049/video/1

item.title: @FinanceLancelot: The next vote on the Clarity Act will be in January 2027, after the new congressional seats take pl...
item.dc:creator: @FinanceLancelot
item.description:
The next vote on the Clarity Act will be in January 2027, after the new congressional seats take place.
The Clarity Act establishes market rules and limits SEC and CFTC oversight for payment stablecoins, specifically when they interact with registered trading entities and 3rd party platforms.
I wouldn't be shocked if this 1st run in $SDEV and $USDE is similar to September 2025, where we had a preliminary rally that sold off, followed by the epic run up as we approach January 2027.
The 1st rally began on 20 Aug and ended 4 Sep 2025. The 2nd rally began on Dec 3rd and ended 9 Jan 2026.
The current rally began on 18 Sep 2026. Will it end 5 Oct 2026?

item.title: @amitisinvesting: The ENTIRE move on the 10-year reversed and then went higher for the day. So if a bad labor market...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
The ENTIRE move on the 10-year reversed and then went higher for the day.
So if a bad labor market report or Treasury buybacks won't get people to buy bonds, it once *again* means that the credit markets need much more evidence that inflation will come down.
The best way to do that might be ending the Iran war but obviously that isn't happening yet.
It also means that something behind the scenes could be perceived as breaking, whether that's a credit event or just increased inflation, and it's creating a further selloff on bonds.
Bessent has to be fuming on this, but the question is...what can he do?

item.title: @amitisinvesting: SEPTEMBER NONFARM PAYROLLS MISS BADLY: - Jobs added were +29K vs +84K expected - Unemployment rate...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
SEPTEMBER NONFARM PAYROLLS MISS BADLY:
- Jobs added were +29K vs +84K expected
- Unemployment rate increases to 4.2% vs 4.1% expected
The 10-year treasury yield just fell 0.77%, the $SPY is up 0.88%, and $BTC is almost at $87K on this news.
Why are yields falling and risk on assets going up if we are seeing unemployment go up and missing on the expected jobs number?
Well, that means the economy might not be as hot as the Fed thinks and we may not need to hike as aggressively as expected.
Bad news, in the eyes of the macro, might be good news again…

item.title: @amitisinvesting: A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY. Here's a full recap: 1. Palantir $PLTR and Arma...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY.
Here's a full recap:
1. Palantir $PLTR and Armada announced a partnership to deliver sovereign AI on modular data center infrastructure manufactured in the U.S. and allied nations. Under the agreement, Palantir named Armada its inaugural Certified Modular Data Center Partner, combining Palantir’s Sovereign AI Operating System with Armada’s Galleon modular data centers, Armada Platform, and Sovereign AI Grid. The joint offering allows enterprises and governments to deploy open-weight AI models on infrastructure they own and control, with the ability to fine-tune models on proprietary data while keeping compute, data, and hardware entirely within their own security boundary. The companies said the modular approach can bring new AI capacity online in months instead of years, addressing growing demand for sovereign AI infrastructure.
2. Nebius $NBIS has acquired Inferize, an AI inference optimization startup, for an undisclosed amount. Inferize’s technology is designed to reduce model “cold starts,” cutting the time GPUs remain idle while models load and new inference capacity comes online. Nebius plans to integrate the technology and team into its Token Factory inference platform to improve GPU utilization, lower inference costs, and serve more AI workloads using the same infrastructure.
3. NVIDIA $NVDA and SoftBank have each completed the final $10B installment of their respective $30B commitments to OpenAI’s latest funding round. The financing totaled $122B in commitments at an $852B valuation and included Amazon’s $50B investment. SoftBank’s total investment in OpenAI has now reached approximately $64.6B, giving it an estimated 13% ownership stake. According to The Information, OpenAI is already targeting another $30B funding round at a valuation of around $1.4T.
4. Netflix $NFLX co-CEO Ted Sarandos said the company “isn’t growing as fast as I want us to,” while noting that some of Netflix’s strategic decisions are intentionally creating headwinds to subscriber growth. He also revealed that live programming accounts for roughly 5% of Netflix’s $20B annual content budget but generates only about 1% of total viewing, underscoring the company’s continued focus on balancing long-term strategic investments with overall engagement.
5. Nike $NKE reported Q1 FY2027 results with EPS of $0.48, beating expectations of $0.43, while revenue missed at $11.21B versus $11.32B expected, down 4% YoY. Gross margin came in stronger than expected at 42.8%, helped by lower warehousing and logistics costs, but weakness persisted across NIKE Direct (-8% YoY), Digital (-13% YoY), and Greater China (-22% YoY). The biggest disappointment was guidance, with Nike forecasting high-single-digit revenue declines for FY2027 and adjusted EPS of $1.15–$1.35, well below the $1.65–$1.67 consensus. Management said it continues to see challenges in Sportswear, Jordan Brand, and Greater China, while rolling out its new Pace operating model to accelerate its long-term turnaround.
6. Broadcom $AVGO has agreed to provide Anthropic with up to $42B in financing tied to its AI infrastructure expansion, according to Anthropic’s IPO prospectus reviewed by Reuters. The facility could fund roughly one-third of Anthropic’s $125.2B five-year TPU compute commitment, and the debt may be convertible into Anthropic equity. Anthropic is also expected to become Broadcom’s largest compute customer in 2027. The filing notes that Broadcom’s dual role as both a hardware supplier and financing partner could create potential conflicts related to pricing and access to compute.
7. Amazon $AMZN plans to expand its in-house delivery network from roughly 23,700 U.S. ZIP codes today to about 39,400 by 2029, according to an internal planning document reviewed by Business Insider. That expansion would allow Amazon to reach approximately 95% of U.S. ZIP codes and 99.9% of customer demand. The plan includes building 165 new delivery stations between 2027 and 2029 and adding roughly 4,500 ZIP codes through its Hub Delivery rural network. The initiative reportedly began under Project Aurelian, a contingency plan created when negotiations with the U.S. Postal Service became uncertain, though Amazon said the projections remain preliminary and could change.
8. The top 10 most active options today by contracts traded were $NVDA with 2.6M contracts, $MU with 1.5M contracts, $TSLA with 1.3M contracts, $AAPL with 1.1M contracts, $SPCX with 786K contracts, $AMZN with 640K contracts, $GOOGL with 637K contracts, $INTC with 582K contracts, $NKE with 561K contracts, and $MSFT with 447K contracts.
9. Oracle $ORCL has reportedly signed a 5-year, $7B AI compute agreement with Tencent, according to the Financial Times. Under the deal, Oracle will provide access to roughly 100,000 advanced AI chips across its Southeast Asia data centers, with about 30% of the contract value paid upfront. Tencent plans to use the capacity to train AI models and expand its portfolio of agentic AI products, as the company accelerates AI infrastructure spending. The investment has already impacted Tencent’s financials, with Q2 infrastructure capex surging 176% YoY to $7.9B and free cash flow turning negative at -$2B for the first time in more than a decade.
10. AI-related companies continue to dominate capital markets, now accounting for roughly 40% of the S&P 500's total market capitalization. In emerging markets, just 3 semiconductor companies make up 28% of the MSCI Emerging Markets Index, while AI-related issuers have represented 49% of all investment-grade bond issuance so far in 2026. The concentration is even more pronounced in private markets, where 87% of year-to-date venture capital funding has gone to AI companies. For comparison, during the 1999 Dot-Com bubble, internet companies accounted for less than 40% of venture capital funding, highlighting the unprecedented concentration of investment flowing into AI today.
11. Since 1928, the S&P 500 has gained an average of 2.1% during the first half of October in U.S. midterm election years, making it the strongest-performing half-month of the fourth quarter. Positive returns occurred 71% of the time over that period, the third-highest hit rate of any half-month in Q4. The seasonal strength follows a historically weak second half of September, which has averaged a 1.1% decline. Momentum has also tended to remain positive later in the quarter, with the second half of October averaging a 0.3% gain and the first half of November delivering an average 1.7% return with a 79% positive hit rate.
12. Bond ETFs have attracted $23B in inflows over the last 5 trading days, accounting for 62% of all ETF net inflows despite representing only about 15% of total ETF assets. Fixed-income funds also made up 6 of the 8 most-purchased ETFs over the period, with investors allocating capital across cash, municipal bonds, high yield, Treasuries, and $TLT. The broad-based demand suggests investors are increasingly positioning around the bond market as yields remain near multi-year highs and volatility persists across asset classes.
WALL STREET IS THE GREATEST SHOW ON EARTH.

item.title: @amitisinvesting: $NKE NIKE CONTINUES TO SHOW SLOWER GROWTH. - $NKE beat on earnings with EPS of $0.48 vs. $0.43 expe...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
$NKE
NIKE CONTINUES TO SHOW SLOWER GROWTH.
- $NKE beat on earnings with EPS of $0.48 vs. $0.43 expected, but revenue missed at $11.2B vs. $11.32B expected, falling 4% YoY.
- NIKE Direct remained a major weak spot, with revenue down 8% YoY and NIKE Brand Digital sales falling 13%.
- China fell into negative growth at -22% YoY.
The worst part was guidance…
- FY2027 guidance came in well below expectations as Nike expects revenue to decline high-single digits vs. ~2.3% expected, while adjusted EPS of $1.15–$1.35 trails the $1.67 consensus estimate.
The stock is now down 75% over the past 5 years…at some point someone steps in?
Right?
Or does Nike continue to be a value trap?

NIKE CONTINUES TO SHOW SLOWER GROWTH.

- $NKE beat on earnings with EPS of $0.48 vs. $0.43 expected, but revenue missed at $11.2B vs. $11.32B expected, falling 4% YoY.

- NIKE Direct remained a major weak spot, with revenue down 8% YoY and NIKE Brand Digital sales falling 13%.

- China fell into negative growth at -22% YoY.

The worst part was guidance…

- FY2027 guidance came in well below expectations as Nike expects revenue to decline high-single digits vs. ~2.3% expected, while adjusted EPS of $1.15–$1.35 trails the $1.67 consensus estimate.

The stock is now down 75% over the past 5 years…at some point someone steps in?

Right?

Or does Nike continue to be a value trap?

The US Bond Market (Bloomberg Agg) was down 2.6% in September.
In the past 30 years, only 5 months had a worse return: 1) September 2022: -4.3% 2) April 2022: -3.8% 3) July 2003: -3.4% 4) August 2022: -2.8% 5) March 2022: -2.8%
For the stock market, losing 2.6% in a month is a nonevent. But for the bond market, this is akin to a crash.

item.description:

On Tuesday the French government said it plans to borrow a record amount on the bond market next year, even as worries about the government's spending has seen borrowing rates hit levels last seen during the 2008 global financial crisis.
Concerns are mounting about France's surging public deficit, borrowing rates and their ability to continue rolling over the debt.
item.content:encoded:

On Tuesday the French government said it plans to borrow a record amount on the bond market next year, even as worries about the government's spending has seen borrowing rates hit levels last seen during the 2008 global financial crisis.

Concerns are mounting about France's surging public deficit, borrowing rates and their ability to continue rolling over the debt.

item.dc:creator: @FinanceLancelot
item.description:
🇫🇷 France's 30 year yield rose to 5.38% today.
They appear to have lost control of the long end of their yield curve, which is something that happens right before a currency / sovereign debt crisis.
The bond markets will force austerity on Britain and France, which will cripple their economic growth, potentially making the debt situation even worse.
France's far-right National Rally (RN) party now have a record 14 seats in the right-wing dominated Senate, effectively quadrupling its number.
The next presidential election is April 18, 2027

item.title: @amitisinvesting: A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY. Here's a full recap: 1. NVIDIA $NVDA unveiled i...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY.
Here's a full recap:
1. NVIDIA $NVDA unveiled its new Open Agent Safety Platform, an open framework designed to continuously monitor and enforce safety for autonomous AI agents across both software and hardware. The platform combines OpenShell, an open-source runtime that sandboxes AI agents with verifiable policies, and NVIDIA Sentry, which runs on BlueField-4 hardware to independently monitor agent behavior and enforce security policies beyond the agent’s control. NVIDIA said the initiative was motivated by recent reports of frontier AI agents escaping evaluation environments and misreporting their actions, arguing that AI agents require an independent trust layer similar to what enabled the modern internet. The company is positioning the platform as an open ecosystem and is inviting frontier AI labs, developers, and infrastructure providers to build on it.
2. Meta $META is launching Meta Enterprise Platform, a new business dedicated to selling its AI tools and services directly to enterprises and developers. The initial offering combines Meta’s enterprise AI stack, including Muse, Meta Business Agent, Muse API, Muse Code, and other products built on the company’s models, agents, and infrastructure to support customer engagement, software development, and broader enterprise workflows. To lead the new division, Meta hired former MongoDB CEO and President CJ Desai as Chief Enterprise Platform Officer, reporting directly to Mark Zuckerberg. Before MongoDB, Desai held leadership roles at Cloudflare and spent nearly 8 years at ServiceNow, including serving as President and COO.
3. Finland President Alexander Stubb said Google $GOOGL will invest at least $15.2B in the country over the next 2 years to expand AI and digital infrastructure. Finland currently has around 50 data centers, with another 25 projects in development, potentially bringing the country's total to 75. The investment further strengthens Finland's position as one of Europe's fastest-growing hubs for AI infrastructure and large-scale data center capacity.
4. Boeing $BA fell 6% after reports that the FAA is delaying certification of the 737 MAX 10 while it reviews a newly discovered software issue that could cause the aircraft’s automated navigation system to fail in certain missed-approach scenarios. According to reports, Southwest and United Airlines have told Boeing they do not want deliveries with the affected software and have instead requested an earlier software version. The certification delay adds another hurdle for Boeing as it works to bring the 737 MAX 10 into commercial service.
5. AMD $AMD has agreed to acquire World Labs, the AI research company founded by Fei-Fei Li, in an $8.2B all-stock transaction. World Labs develops spatial intelligence models capable of generating, reconstructing, and simulating interactive 3D environments from text, images, and video. The acquisition brings World Labs' AI research directly into AMD as the company expands further into reasoning, robotics, simulation, and physical AI. As part of the deal, Fei-Fei Li will join AMD as Executive Vice President and Chief Scientist, reporting directly to CEO Lisa Su. The transaction is expected to close by the end of 2026.
6. The top 10 most active options today by contracts traded were $NVDA with 4.2M contracts, $TSLA with 2.3M contracts, $AAPL with 1.2M contracts, $META with 1.1M contracts, $INTC with 1.1M contracts, $MU with 999K contracts, $AMZN with 728K contracts, $AMD with 704K contracts, $MSFT with 634K contracts, and $SPCX with 622K contracts.
7. NVIDIA $NVDA authorized an additional $150B share repurchase program, the largest increase in share buyback authorization in history, bringing its total remaining authorization to $235B through FY2028. CEO Jensen Huang said the company’s strong cash generation allows NVIDIA to both invest aggressively in the technologies driving the AI transformation and return capital to shareholders. The expanded authorization underscores NVIDIA’s confidence in its long-term growth outlook while providing substantial flexibility for future capital returns.
8. Serious credit card delinquencies continued to rise across several age groups in Q2 2026, with Americans aged 18–29 seeing transitions into 90+ day delinquency climb to 10.1%, up 0.4 percentage points from the prior quarter and the highest level since Q1 2025. The delinquency rate for this group has now more than doubled since Q2 2021. Americans aged 70+ also saw delinquencies rise to 6.3%, the highest since Q3 2011, while the 50–59 age group increased to 6.4%, its highest level since Q4 2024. The data suggests credit stress is continuing to broaden across both younger and older consumers.
9. Retail investors have purchased just $1B of individual U.S. stocks over the last 20 trading days, one of the lowest rolling totals in at least 2 years. In early August, the figure briefly turned negative for the first time since at least October 2024, compared with roughly $20B of 20-day purchases in April 2025. Total retail equity purchases have also slowed sharply, falling to $10B over the last 20 trading days, near their lowest level since at least October 2024. That's down roughly 67% from the $30B recorded over the comparable period in February 2026, highlighting a significant slowdown in retail participation.
10. The 30-year U.S. Treasury Price Return Index has fallen 60% since 2020, dropping to roughly 107, matching its lowest level since 2000. In just 6 years, the index has erased nearly 20 years of gains as the 30-year Treasury yield has surged 478 basis points from its 0.71% intraday low in March 2020. For comparison, the previous largest drawdown over the last 40 years was roughly 35% during the 2008 Financial Crisis. Over the same period, U.S. nominal GDP has grown approximately 63%, highlighting the stark divergence between economic growth and long-duration bond performance.
11. SpaceX $SPCX successfully launched Starship to orbit and deployed its V3 Starlink satellites for the first time, marking Starship’s first revenue-generating mission and a major milestone for the program. According to SpaceX, each V3 Starlink satellite increases the total bandwidth capacity of the entire Starlink constellation by roughly 0.11%. With approximately 11,100 Starlink satellites already in orbit, most of them V2 Mini satellites, future Starship missions carrying up to 60 V3 satellites each could dramatically expand the network’s global capacity while significantly lowering launch costs.
12. U.S. data center IT power demand is projected to surge 755% from 2025 levels, reaching a record 78.57 GW by 2029. Demand is expected to nearly double this year to 17.96 GW, followed by another 97% increase in 2027, as AI infrastructure continues expanding at an unprecedented pace. Between 2026 and 2028, U.S. data centers are expected to require 97 GW of power, but only 21 GW is currently under construction and another 19 GW of grid capacity is available, leaving a potential 57 GW shortfall. The gap is widening as increasingly powerful AI systems consume far more electricity, with servers based on NVIDIA’s Vera Rubin and Rubin Ultra architectures expected to drive a 5x increase in IT power demand between 2025 and 2028.
WALL STREET IS THE GREATEST SHOW ON EARTH.

item.title: @amitisinvesting: pretty weird way to start off the last trading week of September, but then again every week has bee...
item.dc:creator: @amitisinvesting
item.description:
pretty weird way to start off the last trading week of September, but then again every week has been very weird with what’s happening in the macro.
- 10yr jumps to 5.27%, 52 week high
- $NVDA announces $150 buyback and pumps
- $META announces a new AI enterprise business platform and poached the $MDB CEO
- $SPCX completes the first revenue generating Orbital launch for Starship
then after market open…
- semis all dump except $NVDA meaning the confidence of the buyback didn’t extend into the broader sector
- $META dumps 5% on what should be very bullish news for them bringing agents to the enterprise but the semis ALSO dump even though more business agents = more compute so that was weird
- $IGV dumps because Meta is now getting into the enterprise so your software names get hit, but the thing creating the hit (Meta) is down and semis which should benefit from Meta are also down when they usually are up when SaaS is down
- then $SPCX loses all momentum and seemingly takes $TSLA down with it today
no trend or sector trend, just confusion across the board but still a relatively resilient market as $SPY has spent 40 sessions not down 1% or more and even with yields up, the market is not giving out which speaks to how strong the earnings story continues to be.

The one thing you quickly realize, the people in control don't like coming up with new ideas if an old script will suffice.
WW1 was a "preventative war" against the Russian railway building (China Belt and Road initiative 2026)
WW2 was a "preventative war" to stop Japanese expansion (Iran 2026).
The common denominator here is both world wars were fought over global trade routes, exactly what is happening right now.
In order to convince the public these wars are worth fighting, they need a false flag attack.
Think: • 9/11 for the Gulf Wars • Gulf of Tonkin incident 1964 for the Vietnam war. • The RMS Lusitania sinking on May 7, 1915 where Britain deliberately staged the attack to draw the United States into WW1
Prior to WW2, the U.S. deliberately cut off 90% of Japan's oil supply leaving Japan no choice but to attack.
The U.S. deliberately moved all of their older WW1 ships to Pearl Harbor, ensuring maximum casualties, while pulling all 3 aircraft carriers away mere days before the false flag.
They also made sure there were plenty cameras on site, so films of the destruction could be shown in every movie theatre across America.
Current public support of the Iran war is at the lowest levels since 1940.
Now ask yourself, what false flag could be used to flip that switch in public support?
